What is Binance Margin Trading?

Binance Margin Trading is a feature on the Binance cryptocurrency exchange that allows users to borrow funds against their existing holdings to trade with leverage, to potentially increase profits. Maximum leverage varies by trading pair and account type. While Cross Margin can go up to 20x and Isolated up to 10x, many pairs have lower caps based on risk level and liquidity.

While leveraged trading enables traders to amplify profits, it also carries a high risk of potential loss due to leverage and potential liquidation if margin levels fall below thresholds.

To simplify margin trading, Binance offers tools like auto-transfer, auto-borrow, and auto-repay. Auto-transfer automates fund transfers between Spot and Margin wallets, auto-borrow automates borrowing funds when placing margin orders, and auto-repay repays loans with proceeds from closed trades.

Start margin trading on Binance today and earn monetary rewards to boost your trading capital.

What are the Pros and Cons of Margin Trading on Binance?

The pros of margin trading on Binance are listed below:

  • Access to More Capital: You can trade with more than what you have. Once you move assets into your margin account, you get access to borrowed funds. This lets you enter bigger trades with less capital.
  • Wide Range of Trading Pairs and Options: You’re not limited to one or two coins. Binance supports 600+ margin trading pairs, so traders are not stuck waiting for one market to move.
  • Updates Borrowing and Margin Level: The platform updates everything while you trade. You see your margin level, how much you’ve borrowed, and how close you are to liquidation as the price changes. It keeps you informed without needing extra tools.
  • Built-in Risk Management Tools Like Stop Loss (SL) and Take Profit (TP): You can set stop loss and take profit on every margin trade. Stop loss and take profit are limits set on trades (market or pending) so that they are automatically closed at an expected gain or a minimal loss. This helps you manage risk and plan exits.
  • Direct Integration: Margin trading happens right inside the Binance ecosystem. Whether you are trading through the Binance app or website, there is no need to use third-party tools or open multiple tabs. Everything from transferring funds to repaying loans is handled in Binance Exchange.
  • Customer Support: Binance offers 24/7 support through live chat and email. If you need answers to frequently asked questions, you can get help through the live chat or the FAQ section. However, if you need help with more complex issues, you can contact the support team via email.

In addition to these channels, Binance is popular for providing users with extensive learning tools, including articles, videos, tutorials and other educational content through Binance Academy. With these materials, you can easily learn how to trade on the exchange and get answers to your questions at all times.

The cons of margin trading on Binance are listed below:

  • Potential Losses and Risk of Liquidation: When the trade moves against you and your margin level drops, Binance starts to close your position. This can lead to losing more than you expected. Also, if the margin level drops below the set range, Binance can forcibly close (liquidate) your position.
  • Borrowed Funds are Not Free: As long as you keep the position open, interest is added to what you owe. The longer you hold, the more it costs. Nevertheless, this won’t be much of a problem if your trades are profitable.
  • Crypto Markets Move Mast. A sudden dip can bring your margin down before you have time to act. Even if the price recovers later, your position might already be gone.
  • Leverage Goes Both Ways: While it can help grow profits, it also means small mistakes can turn into large losses. So, you need to keep an eye on your trades at all times.

How Does Margin Trading Work in Binance?

Margin trading on Binance works by allowing users to borrow funds to increase their trading capital and amplify potential returns. First, you transfer funds into your margin wallet. That becomes the base Binance uses to calculate how much you can borrow. And the higher the value of your deposit, the more leverage you can access, up to 10x leverage on Isolated Margin and up to 20x on Cross Margin.

Next, you choose the trading pair and open a position. You can go long if you believe the asset will rise, or short if you expect a drop. Now, you’re trading with more than you own; both your original deposit and the borrowed funds are combined in that trade. If the price moves in your favor, you close the trade, repay the borrowed amount with interest, and keep the profit.

However, if the market turns against your position, your margin level starts to fall. If it drops too far, Binance can liquidate your position automatically. This means your assets will be sold off to recover the loan. 

Binance offers different modes for margin trading orders. You can either borrow and repay funds manually or allow the system automatically borrow the required assets based on maximum leverage when placing an order. For the automated repayment, the system automatically uses the proceeds to repay the borrowed amount after closing the trade.

Please note: Borrowed funds accrue interest charged hourly. Additionally, when repaying loans, you must repay the same asset borrowed (e.g., if BTC was borrowed, repayment must be in BTC).

What are the Types of Margin Trading on Binance?

The two types of margin trading on Binance are Cross Margin and Isolated Margin. Here is a rundown of the difference between Cross vs. Isolated Margin.

  1. Cross Margin: In Cross Margin mode, all the balances in your margin account are pooled together as collateral for all your open margin positions. This means that if one position is losing, other assets in your margin account can be used to cover margin requirements, potentially preventing the liquidation of a single position.

However, the risk of Binance Cross Margin trading is that losses in one trade can affect all your margin positions since the collateral is shared across all trades. This mode is suitable for traders who want to maximize the use of their total margin balance and are comfortable with the risk spreading across positions.

  1. Isolated Margin: In Isolated Margin mode, each trading pair has its own separate margin account with a specific amount of collateral allocated to it. Here, only specific cryptocurrencies can be transferred in, held, and borrowed in a specific isolated margin account. For instance, if you want to invest in ETHUSDT isolated margin account, only ETH and USDT are accessible.

If the market moves against a particular trade, only the collateral allocated to that trade is at risk of liquidation, protecting the rest of your margin balance from being affected. Unlike the Cross Margin mode, this mode allows better risk management on individual trades and is suitable for traders who want to limit their risk exposure per position.

What are the Fees and Interest Rates for Binance Margin Trading?

Binance charges two main costs when trading on margin, the regular trading fee and interest on the borrowed funds. The trading fee depends on your VIP level and whether the order is a maker or taker. Most users on a basic account pay around 0.1 percent per trade. That amount can drop with higher trading volume or if there’s enough BNB in the account to qualify for up to 20% BNB holders discount.

However, interest is charged separately and only applies to the amount borrowed. The rate depends on the coin, your VIP level, and can change depending on market activity. Interest starts the moment the loan is active and continues until the balance is fully repaid. The longer the trade stays open, the more interest builds up.

Access a $100 welcome bonus, live interest rates, and flexible borrowing with Binance margin trading.

What Are the Borrowing Limits for Binance Margin Trading?

Borrowing limits in Binance margin trading depend on the asset, the margin mode, and your VIP level. Traders with more trading volume (high VIP status) are eligible for more borrow limits compared to regular users. Below is the loan rate and borrowing limit for regular traders.

Aside from the VIP level, each coin available for margin has a set borrowing cap. Assets that are traded more often and have more liquidity typically allow higher limits, while smaller or less liquid coins cap borrowing at lower levels.

In cross margin, all assets in the margin wallet work together as collateral. That means borrowing power is based on the total value of everything in that wallet. As long as the combined balance holds up, larger positions are possible. However, if one position starts losing, it puts pressure on the entire account.

Now, the isolated margin treats each trade separately. When opening a position, only the funds assigned to that trade back the loan. That keeps risk limited to that one position, but the borrowing room is smaller because it’s tied only to that pair.

The actual borrowing amount also depends on your margin level, the ratio between your assets and what you’ve borrowed plus interest. If your margin level drops near liquidation, Binance may restrict additional borrowing to protect the platform and reduce your exposure. The platform adjusts limits in real time when the market moves sharply.

To know exactly how much you can borrow, the Margin Data page on Binance shows live limits for each asset.

What is the Difference Between Spot and Margin Trading on Binance?

Spot trading on Binance is a straightforward transaction where you buy or sell cryptocurrency using your own funds. When you place a spot order, you exchange one asset for another immediately or when your limit is filled. For example, if you want to buy Bitcoin using USDT, the full amount must already be in your wallet. Once the order is executed, the asset becomes yours without any debt or additional obligations.

Margin trading, on the other hand, involves borrowing funds from Binance to increase your buying power. You still start with your own capital, but the platform allows you to borrow more and open a larger position than your actual balance would allow. This means if your trade goes in the right direction, the gains and losses can be much bigger than in spot trading.

Another key difference is the way positions are managed on spot vs. margin trading. Spot trades do not require monitoring beyond their entry and exit strategy. There’s no debt, no interest, and no liquidation risk. In margin trading, each open position is tied to the loaned funds and is constantly monitored by the system. If the margin level falls too low, Binance can automatically liquidate your position to recover the borrowed amount.

Spot trading is for users who want direct ownership of crypto and less risk. Margin trading is designed for those who are confident in market direction and want to trade with leverage. The risk is higher, but so is the reward.

What is the Difference Between Futures and Margin Trading on Binance?

Margin trading on Binance involves borrowing funds to trade larger amounts than your actual balance allows. You put down a portion of the trade’s value as collateral and borrow the rest from the platform. You are charged interest on the borrowed funds, and your assets serve as security. You still own the assets you buy, and the trades happen on the spot market. That means you’re buying or selling real cryptocurrencies.

Binance Futures trading works differently. You are not trading actual coins. Instead, you are trading contracts that track the price of cryptocurrencies. You don’t own the asset, but you can still profit from its movement. These contracts allow you to bet on future prices of crypto assets.

There’s no interest charged like in margin trading, but there is a funding fee that shifts between buyers and sellers based on market conditions. One similarity you will see in Binance margin or futures, is leverage and liquidation risk. Futures contracts also offer leverage, which is often higher than margin trading (up to 125x), but the risk of liquidation is greater too.

How to Margin Trade Crypto on Binance?

Here is a step-by-step guide on how to margin trade crypto on Binance.

Step 1: Enable Margin Trading on the Binance App or Website

Start by logging in to your Binance account. From the main dashboard, navigate to your wallet and click on the margin section. If you haven’t, you will be prompted to complete identity verification and accept Binance’s margin trading terms.

Step 2: Transfer Funds into Your Margin Wallet

To begin trading, move funds from your spot wallet into your margin wallet. This amount will serve as your collateral. Based on your deposit value, Binance calculates how much you can borrow. The more you fund your wallet, the higher your borrowing power.

Step 3: Borrow and Choose a Trading Pair

With funds in your margin wallet, select the crypto pair you want to trade. Binance allows you to borrow additional assets to increase your position size. You can then decide whether to go long or short depending on the market direction. If you expect the asset to rise in value, you go long. If you expect it to fall, you go short.

Step 4: Place Your Order and Monitor Your Margin Level

After choosing your trading pair and borrowing funds, place your order. Binance gives you the option to use either cross or isolated margin. Cross margin uses all the funds in your margin wallet to protect open trades, while isolated margin limits risk to the specific trade. 

Once your position is open, monitor your margin level closely to avoid liquidation. If it falls below the required threshold, Binance will liquidate your position to recover the borrowed funds.

How to Set Up a Margin Account on Binance?

To use Binance Margin for trading, you need to activate margin trading on your account.  Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to set up a margin account on Binance from scratch.

Step 1: Log In and Complete Identity Verification: Start by signing in to your Binance account. If you don’t have one yet, create an account via the Binance app or official website using a valid email address and a strong password.

Then, complete the KYC verification process. This step is necessary before you can access any margin-related features. If you’re new to the platform, consider checking out a detailed Binance review first to understand how it works and whether it fits your trading goals.

Now is the moment to join Binance and try margin trading.

Step 2: Navigate to the Margin Trading Section: Once your identity has been verified, head to the “Wallet” section at the top of the screen. From there, select “Margin” and you will be taken to the Binance Margin interface. You’ll be required to complete a short quiz about the risks of margin trading before continuing.

Step 3: Enable Margin Trading: After completing the quiz, you can enable your margin wallet. Binance will ask you to confirm that you understand the risks involved. Once you accept the terms, your margin wallet becomes active, and you can start transferring funds into it.

Step 4: Transfer Funds and Begin Trading: Move funds from your spot wallet into your margin wallet to begin trading. Once the funds reflect, you can borrow assets and start margin trading across supported pairs.

If you’re opening your first margin account, Binance occasionally offers exclusive bonuses to new users, including lower trading fees and rewards on your first trades. Check out this Binance referral code article to see how these bonuses work and how to qualify.

How to Qualify for Binance Margin Trading?

Before you can borrow funds or place trades using leverage on Binance, you need to meet a few key requirements. These steps help protect your funds and ensure that you understand the risks involved.

  1. Complete Identity Verification

This is the first and most crucial step. Binance needs to know who is using the platform. You’ll be asked to upload a government-issued ID and a clear photo of yourself. The identity verification process enables Binance to comply with international regulations and provides an additional layer of security for your account.

  1. Pass the Margin Trading Quiz

After your identity has been verified, Binance will prompt you to take a short quiz. The questions focus on how margin trading works, the risks of using borrowed funds, and what can happen when the market turns against you. The purpose of this quiz is to check that you understand the basics before you start trading with leverage. You’ll need to pass this quiz before Binance will unlock margin trading features for your account.

  1. Agree to the Margin Account Terms

Once the quiz is done, you will be shown a set of terms and conditions. This is where Binance outlines how the margin system works, what happens during liquidation, and how interest is calculated on borrowed funds. Accepting these terms means you are aware of your responsibilities and the platform’s policies.

  1. Check for Regional Restrictions

Binance does not offer margin trading in every country. Specific locations are blocked due to legal or regulatory reasons. Even if your identity is verified, you won’t be able to activate margin trading if Binance has restrictions in your region. To avoid confusion, it’s a good idea to check Binance’s list of supported countries before opening a margin trading account.

  1. Keep a Clean Account Record

Binance may withhold margin access if your account has unresolved issues. This could include suspicious activity, incomplete verification, or flagged transactions. If you’ve used the platform for a while, keeping your account history clean can help avoid delays when applying for margin access.

Take advantage of new user rewards and start trading with 10% fee discounts on Binance margin pairs.

How to Transfer Collateral on Binance Margin?

Below is a step-by-step guide on how to transfer collateral on Binance margin 

Step 1. Log in to Your Binance Account: Begin by signing in and navigating to the Wallet section. From the available options, select Margin Wallet. This is where you’ll find your available balance, borrowed funds, and margin level.

Step 2. Click the Transfer Button: Inside your margin wallet, locate and click the Transfer button. This will open a short form that allows you to transfer funds internally from your Spot Wallet to your Margin Wallet.

Step 3. Choose the Crypto You Want to Use: Choose which asset you want to transfer. Binance allows you to use coins like Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT, or BNB as collateral. Your choice here depends on what you already own and what you’re comfortable using.

Step 4. Enter the Amount and Confirm: Type in how much you’d like to transfer. The more you transfer, the more you can borrow, so keep your risk level in mind. After checking everything, confirm the transfer.

Step 5. Wait for Instant Confirmation: Your collateral will reflect in your margin wallet almost right away. Since the funds are being moved within Binance, there’s no fee or delay. Once the transfer is done, you’re ready to borrow and begin margin trading.

What Are the Best Margin Trading Tips for Binance Beginners?

Here are six beginner-friendly tips to help you manage risk and build confidence while margin trading on Binance.

  1. Start Small and Observe: Margin trading offers leverage, which can multiply both profits and losses. That’s why it’s better to begin with a small trade and invest only an amount you’re willing to lose. Use this early stage to observe how price movements affect your borrowed position and how quickly markets can change.
  2. Use Isolated Margin Mode: For new traders, using isolated margin is a safer starting point. It allows you to contain your risk in one position, rather than tying multiple trades together. If things go wrong, you only lose the funds assigned to that trade. That’s different from cross margin, where one bad trade could drain your entire margin account.
  3. Don’t Borrow the Maximum Limit: Just because you can borrow more doesn’t mean you should. Margin gives you access to extra funds, but it’s smart to borrow only what you can manage. Going all-in reduces your cushion and increases your risk of liquidation. Keep your leverage low, especially in the beginning, until you’re more comfortable managing price swings.
  4. Watch Your Margin Level: Your margin level tells you how healthy your position is. If it falls too low, Binance will automatically liquidate your trade to recover the borrowed amount. That’s why it’s essential to monitor your open position often.
  5. Set Clear Stop-Losses: Markets can move fast, and it’s easy to get caught off guard. A stop-loss acts as your safety brake; it closes your trade when prices fall below a certain point. This tool is especially helpful when you’re not watching the charts 24/7. Always plan your exit before you enter the trade.
  6. Reflect on Every Trade: After closing a trade, take time to go back and review it. Ask yourself what worked, what didn’t, and what you would do differently in the future. These small reflections help you spot patterns and avoid repeating mistakes.

Explore Binance’s built-in margin trading tools while earning from exclusive deals.

Does Binance U.S Offer Margin Trading?

No, Binance US does not offer margin trading. This is mainly due to stricter financial regulations in the United States. Margin trading involves borrowing funds to trade larger amounts, which adds a higher level of risk. US regulators have tighter rules around this kind of trading to protect retail and institutional investors.

Can I Withdraw Margin Money?

No, you cannot withdraw borrowed margin funds on Binance. The money is strictly for trading and stays in your margin account until you repay it. However, any unused funds you personally deposited, not borrowed, can be moved back to your spot wallet and withdrawn.

title: An attempt to fix self-custody. Will Bron succeed?
summary: On 29 October, attackers reportedly linked to North Korea moved about $6.3 billion out of Binance's hot wallets in roughly twenty minutes. Binance has said its users will not bear the loss. Customers of smaller platforms have rarely been so fortunate, and every hack like this revives the same advice...
content:
Skip to content

On 29 October, attackers reportedly linked to North Korea moved about $6.3 billion out of Binance's hot wallets in roughly twenty minutes. Binance has said its users will not bear the loss. Customers of smaller platforms have rarely been so fortunate, and every hack like this revives the same advice: take your coins off the exchange and hold them yourself.

The advice is sound, but this year has shown how hard it is to follow well. I went looking for the best options out there and found Bron, which looks to me like a non-custodial wallet done right. Below, I will explain why.

When the safe wallet is not safe

In October, Ledger confirmed that criminals had fitted hidden implants to some of its devices and resold them through CryptoBilis, one of its authorised resellers in Southeast Asia. On-chain analysts put the losses at more than $90 million.

The weakness sat outside the device: in 24 words that work for anyone who sees them, and in the knowledge of who owns them and where they live. A seed phrase is a single point of failure. Whoever reads it owns your assets, and so does whoever can force you to recite it.

How institutions actually hold crypto

Institutions start from a different assumption: that any single person, device or location will eventually fail. With multi-party computation (MPC), the signing key exists only as separate shards held by different parties, and no single shard can move funds.

On top of the cryptography sits governance. Transfers above a limit need a second approver. New destinations wait before they are trusted. Changes to the rules are slow and visible. Recovery is a documented procedure, not a piece of paper in a drawer.

From Copper to Bron

Dmitry Tokarev founded Copper, which launched in London in 2018 with MPC custody built for institutions and today serves banks, asset managers, trading firms and exchanges. In 2024, he stepped down as CEO and founded Bron, which today brings the same architecture to private individuals, families and family offices.

In Bron, the signing key is split into three shards. One lives on the customer’s device, protected by its secure hardware and biometrics. One is held by Bron. The third is held by Qrypt, an independent recovery provider contracted on behalf of the customer. Any two shards can sign a transaction or restore the third one, but no single shard can move anything. There is no seed phrase to write down or be forced to recite, and nothing for an implant to read off a screen. If Bron ever disappeared, the customer would automatically rebuild the private key using their own shard and Qrypt’s, without any dependency on Bron.

Recovery without an ID

Lose your device and you lose nothing. If you still have another trusted device, you approve the new one from it. If you have lost every device, you recover with FaceScan or with codes from two Guardians, people you trust, after a 48-hour security delay.

True to the crypto ethos, none of these routes asks for a government-issued ID, because one is not needed to prove that you are you: your face, or the codes from two Guardians you appointed yourself, is the best proof out there. Guardians never see your balances or transactions, and Bron does not store a photo of your face: FaceScan, powered by iProov, keeps only an encrypted template that cannot be turned back into a picture once it is created. Ledger Recover, by contrast, requires a passport or national identity card to subscribe, verifies your identity online before it restores anything, and charges a subscription fee, while Bron is free.

Inheritance without handing over keys

A seed phrase reaches heirs only if someone hands it over, which means trusting them with everything today or hoping they find it tomorrow. With Bron’s digital inheritance, customers invite beneficiaries in advance. They set up their own access but see no balances or transactions. Only a beneficiary can start the inheritance process, which then runs for 12 months, or six if two of the Guardians provide their codes. Everyone is notified by email, and the owner, any Guardian or any beneficiary can cancel at any time, so that no malicious beneficiary can take advantage of the owner. When the delay ends, the beneficiaries who joined become owners of the workspace.

Note that the inheritance process does not replace your will. It does, however, give your will something it can point to, which is the most important part.

Security is also physical

Hacks make the headlines, but a growing threat to wealthy holders is a stranger at the door. Interestingly, Bron’s engineers have thought about this too.

Hidden accounts stay invisible until you type their six-digit PIN, so a forced unlock shows only what you choose to show. Resetting a PIN takes 24 hours, so even if you are forced to do it, the wallet keeps you protected.

All of the above, however, does not protect you from kidnapping. Bron has a policy engine to deal with exactly that. Any transfer above a set amount can be made to wait, or to need a second approval from a family member or an adviser who can approve but cannot move funds. The first transfer to a new address can be held until someone approves it. Changes to users, limits or the address book wait at least 48 hours or need approval. Best of all, these controls work across every chain: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Tron, Hyperliquid, Ripple, Zcash, Gram and many others, including all the L2s.

Holding your own assets was meant to remove the need to trust an exchange. Done properly, it removes the need to trust any single thing.

If done right, self-custody should outlive the device, the thief and, in time, its owner.

title: Bitcoin Is ‘Running on Empty’ as Price Bets and Hedges Shift: Glassnode
summary: Bitcoin’s weakening market structure has prompted fresh scrutiny of its next move, with Glassnode’s Nov. 11, 2026, report warning that capital is departing even as larger investors accumulate. Meanwhile, options traders are hedging downside exposure, and prediction markets are assigning increasingly...
content:
Bitcoin’s weakening market structure has prompted fresh scrutiny of its next move, with Glassnode’s Nov. 11, 2026, report warning that capital is departing even as larger investors accumulate. Meanwhile, options traders are hedging downside exposure, and prediction markets are assigning increasingly cautious probabilities to bitcoin’s recovery.

Key Takeaways

  • Glassnode’s latest assessment exposes a curious contradiction beneath bitcoin’s seemingly exhausted market.
  • Options traders are preparing for several possibilities, but a looming expiration could complicate their positioning.
  • Millions of dollars in prediction market activity reveal a striking divide between bitcoin’s near-term prospects and its more ambitious price targets.

Analytics Firm Glassnode Warns Capital Keeps Leaving

Glassnode published its latest assessment on the social media platform X on Wednesday, Nov. 11, under the rather ominous title “Running on Empty.” Its central argument is that bitcoin’s price recovery prospects are being constrained by disappearing liquidity, weakening American demand, and mounting pressure on relatively recent investors.

“Bitcoin has slipped below the short-term holder cost basis at $75.6K and trails stocks, while the capital that could lift it keeps leaving,” Glassnode explained. The analytics firm added:

“Stablecoin supply is shrinking at the fastest pace since June 2022, the ETFs are net sellers, and bitcoin trades at a discount on Coinbase.”

Indeed, Glassnode estimates that stablecoin supply contracted by $14.2 billion over 30 days, while U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) experienced $1.6 billion in net redemptions across 20 trading sessions. Coinbase’s bitcoin premium has also remained negative, reaching its deepest discount since February.

Meanwhile, approximately 35% of short-term holder coins remain profitable, compared with nearly all such holdings at September’s high. Glassnode identified considerable overhead supply extending toward $83,600, potentially complicating recovery attempts as underwater investors seek opportunities to exit.

Nevertheless, the situation is hardly one-sided. “On the other side, the slide has cleared most long leverage near price, bids outweigh asks in the order book, and two large wallet cohorts have started accumulating,” the firm observed. Wallets holding 100 to 1,000 BTC and 1,000 to 10,000 BTC have resumed accumulation, although smaller investors and the largest holders continue distributing.

Glassnode identified substantial resting bids between $68,000 and $72,500, alongside a liquidation concentration between $59,500 and $62,600. Above prevailing prices, comparatively sparse order-book liquidity extends toward $84,000, while short liquidations cluster near $87,500. “The September high was the first higher high since the 2025 all-time high, and that trend change holds as long as price stays above the June low at $58.5K,” Glassnode stated.

Its immediate technical markers include $75,600 for the short-term holder cost basis, $77,500 for the true market mean, and $77,800 for bitcoin’s election-day closing level.

Are Bitcoin Options Traders Preparing for a Recovery or Further Trouble?

Compounding on what Glassnode sees right now, Coinglass derivatives figures reveal a market balancing longer-term optimism against immediate downside protection. Bitcoin options open interest stands at 439,966 BTC, approximately $33 billion, with calls representing 55.72% and puts accounting for 44.28%. The resulting put-to-call ratio of 0.79 suggests upside exposure retains a modest advantage.

The largest options exchange by volume, Coinbase’s Deribit, dominates the largest outstanding contracts. Its Nov. 13 $81,000 call carries 8,305.9 BTC in open interest, followed by the Dec. 25 $80,000 call with 8,113.9 BTC and the $100,000 call with 6,612.7 BTC. December positioning also includes 6,520.6 BTC in $60,000 puts, 5,842.1 BTC in $120,000 calls, 5,518.8 BTC in $40,000 puts, and 5,403.9 BTC in $90,000 calls. Another 5,200.8 BTC sits in Nov. 13 $84,000 calls.

The November $81,000 and $84,000 contracts collectively represent approximately $1 billion in notional exposure, although bitcoin would need a substantial recovery before Friday’s expiration. Recent trading presents a more defensive picture. Across 45,210 BTC in 24-hour options volume, puts accounted for 50.32%, narrowly exceeding calls at 49.68%.

Activity concentrated around Nov. 12-13 contracts struck between $72,000 and $75,500. Particularly active were Deribit’s $72,000 and $73,000 puts, with respective volumes of 730.3 BTC and 715.8 BTC. Other notable contracts included Deribit’s Nov. 27 $100,000 call at 868.3 BTC and Dec. 25 $50,000 put at 673.8 BTC.

Historically, options open interest peaked near $65 billion in October 2025, declined rapidly toward $25 billion after December’s expiration, and briefly recovered to approximately $53 billion in September 2026. Deribit trading volume likewise reached approximately $11.5 billion during September, compared with roughly $5 billion amid this month’s retreat.

What Are Prediction Markets Saying About Bitcoin’s Next Price?

Prediction markets offer another perspective, with four markets across Polymarket and Kalshi reflecting substantial differences between near-term price touches and year-end outcomes. Polymarket’s November bitcoin price market has attracted $5.17 million across 28 targets. Traders assign a 91% probability to touching $75,000, 62% to $77,500, and 39% to $80,000. Conversely, downside probabilities stand at 73% for $72,500, 50% for $70,000, and 18% for $65,000. Reaching $100,000 commands just 1%.

Polymarket’s broader 2026 price-touch market has accumulated $84.26 million. Its probabilities include 61% for $70,000, 34% for $65,000, and 20% for $60,000. Upside targets receive 18% for $90,000, 6% for $100,000, and less than 1% for $250,000. At the same time, Kalshi’s November maximum-price market, with $1.34 million in volume, assigns 19% to exceeding $82,500, 15% to $85,000, and 8% to $87,500.

Kalshi’s separate $46.75 million year-end settlement market favors a narrower outcome. The $70,000-$74,999.99 bracket leads at 18.9%, followed by $75,000-$79,999.99 at 18.5%, and $65,000-$69,999.99 at 13%. Crucially, these contracts measure different outcomes. Polymarket’s price-touch contracts settle when specified thresholds are reached, while Kalshi’s year-end market concerns bitcoin’s actual closing range.

Taken together, Glassnode’s latest liquidity warning, defensive options activity, and seemingly bearish prediction market probabilities portray an uncertain market rather than an inevitable collapse. Large holders are accumulating, yet broader capital flows remain unfavorable. Bitcoin’s immediate challenge is not simply attracting buyers, but demonstrating that renewed demand can outlast the selling pressure already embedded in its market structure.

title: Bitmine Reports $6.3B Net Loss as Ether Plunges 44% During Fiscal Year
summary: Bitmine Immersion Technologies reported a $6.23 billion unrealized loss on its cryptocurrency holdings during its 2026 fiscal year, as a steep decline in ether’s price weighed heavily on the company’s rapidly expanding digital asset treasury. According to its annual filing with the SEC, Bitmine reco...
content:
Bitmine Immersion Technologies reported a $6.23 billion unrealized loss on its cryptocurrency holdings during its 2026 fiscal year, as a steep decline in ether’s price weighed heavily on the company’s rapidly expanding digital asset treasury.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitmine reported a $6.23 billion unrealized cryptocurrency loss and a $6.31 billion annual net loss, as Ethereum fell approximately 44% during its fiscal year ended Aug. 31, 2026.
  • Annual revenue surged to $124.8 million, primarily from Ethereum staking, but operating expenses and cryptocurrency valuation losses overwhelmed those gains.
  • Bitmine increased its holdings to 6.07 million ETH by Nov. 8, reaching approximately 4.97% of Ethereum’s circulating supply, while generating an estimated $309 million in annualized staking revenue.

According to its annual filing with the SEC, Bitmine recorded a net loss of $6.31 billion for the fiscal year ended Aug. 31, 2026, reversing a $348.6 million profit in the previous year. The unrealized cryptocurrency loss compared with an $805 million unrealized gain in fiscal 2025.

Ethereum’s price fell approximately 44% during the reporting period, dropping from $4,391.91 on Aug. 31, 2025, to $2,467.65 on Aug. 31, 2026, according to historical data. The decline substantially reduced the value of Bitmine’s ether holdings as the company continued accumulating the cryptocurrency.

The losses were largely attributable to ether. Bitmine’s filing identified approximately $6.22 billion in negative fair-value adjustments to its ETH holdings during the year, alongside a much smaller loss on bitcoin.

As of Aug. 31, Bitmine held 5,901,837 ETH with a cost basis of $19.95 billion and a fair market value of $14.56 billion. That represented a roughly $5.39 billion shortfall relative to the acquisition cost of its remaining ether holdings. The figure differs from its annual unrealized loss because the company continued purchasing and receiving ETH throughout the reporting period.

Despite the losses, Bitmine reported substantial revenue growth following its transition from bitcoin mining toward an ether-focused treasury and staking business. Annual revenue increased to $124.8 million from $6.1 million in fiscal 2025, including $121.4 million generated from staking and validation activities. The company began native ETH staking in Nov. 2025, establishing a new source of recurring income from its cryptocurrency holdings.

However, general and administrative expenses reached $376.9 million, exceeding total revenue. Bitmine also recorded $143.7 million in losses on derivative contracts and a $22.9 million decline in the value of its investment in Eightco Holdings.

Bitmine Nears 5% ETH Milestone

The financial results come as Bitmine approaches its long-standing goal of controlling 5% of ether’s circulating supply.

As Bitcoin.com News reported Monday, the company purchased another 9,587 ETH worth approximately $20 million, bringing its holdings to 6,070,092 tokens as of Nov. 8. That represented roughly 4.97% of Ethereum’s circulating supply, leaving Bitmine approximately 40,000 ETH short of its target. The firm said it plans to stop buying ETH once it reaches that milestone.

Chairman Tom Lee has maintained an optimistic outlook despite the market downturn. In the company’s latest update, Lee praised Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin’s recent characterization of ETH as a store of value, describing the shift as a significant development for Ethereum’s role in tokenized finance.

Bitmine also reported approximately 5.23 million ETH staked as of Nov. 8, generating an estimated $309 million in annualized staking revenue at prevailing yields.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin.com News previously reported that Bitmine repurchased approximately 22.9 million of its own shares for $399.6 million during 2026, reflecting management’s view that its stock was undervalued relative to the company’s assets.

The latest annual figures underscore the financial risks of Bitmine’s concentrated ether strategy. While staking provides recurring revenue, fluctuations in ETH’s market price can produce multibillion-dollar changes in reported earnings, even without the company selling its holdings.

title: Solana Privacy Rings Go Live on Mainnet With Encrypted Transfers and Private DeFi
summary:
Key Takeaways: Helius has officially deployed its Solana Privacy Rings on mainnet, bringing the feature directly into Solana. The first permissionless Ring makes assets and transaction amounts hidden while wallet
The post Solana Privacy Rings Go Live on Mainnet With Encrypted Transfers and Private D...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Helius has officially deployed its Solana Privacy Rings on mainnet, bringing the feature directly into Solana.
  • The first permissionless Ring makes assets and transaction amounts hidden while wallet addresses are visible.
  • Unique Rings for institutions are scheduled for Q4 2026, featuring customizable compliance rules and an auditor feature.

Helius has announced the release of Solana Privacy Rings, bringing programmable privacy to payments, DeFi and upcoming institutional applications, on mainnet. The system maintains balances and transfer amounts as encrypted zero knowledge proofs, which are yet to be performed natively on Solana.

  • Solana Gets Native Confidential Transfers
  • Privacy Extends Beyond Payments
    • Custom Rings Target Institutional Crypto Use
    • Helius Opens Privacy APIs to Solana Developers

Solana Gets Native Confidential Transfers

Privacy Rings are shielded pools, directly implemented on Solana, that are programmable. The default permissionless Ring encrypts the amount and assets being transferred, but public displays of wallet addresses. They can decipher their own balance with a viewing key.

It is compatible with SOL, SPL and Token-2022 assets. Private transactions take place right on Solana, while private data stays on the Solana network ledger for the benefit of the user.

Helius claims the zero-knowledge proofs can verify private transactions in just milliseconds, which means that users can now transfer funds without having to wait for a separate sidechain or external privacy network.

Read More: Reflect Lets Anyone Launch a Solana Stablecoin in Under a Minute With Shared Yield

Privacy Extends Beyond Payments

Developers can even implement more elaborate applications using private escrows. The initial use cases include private swaps, lending, staking, yield products and conditional payments, Helius said. With a single transaction, private balances can communicate with other programs on Solana and be liquidity providers to each other.

Helius says that the system is already being used by Decrypt, Ore and Aurora Intents. Other teams on integrations are BackPack, DFlow, Jupiter, Squads and Titan.

Custom Rings Target Institutional Crypto Use

Helius is also working on Custom Rings for financial institutions requiring privacy without compromising compliance regulations.

Participants can be visible or invisible, and institutions will be able to specify their approved participants, block addresses and block activity or require added signatures.

Auditor keys may be provided to audit to be able to view balances and transactions but not control funds. Some transactions can also be selectively disclosed using dedicated viewing keys.

Custom Rings are currently being audited, and its launch on the Solana Mainnet is planned for Q4 2026.

Helius Opens Privacy APIs to Solana Developers

Helius APIs and software development kits enable developers to start integrating Privacy Rings.

Its tooling consists of TypeScript and Rust SDKs, Blueshift privacy-aware RPC methods and zero-knowledge development tools. Helius is also in the process of developing an on-chain wallet which will allow for public and private balances.

The core programs and zero-knowledge circuits have already undergone audits by Certora, ZK Security and OtterSec, and the formal verification process will persist until the end of 2026.

title: OKXICE moves ahead with tokenized stocks as blue chips push back
summary: The Nov. 23 debut puts a new SEC exemption to the test as Nasdaq pursues its own tokenized stock plans after warning that trading across platforms could fragment liquidity.
content:
Crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) are set to launch tokenized stock trading on Nov. 23, despite objections from 67 companies to having their shares listed and warnings from Nasdaq that trading across disconnected platforms could fragment liquidity.

The venture, known as OKXICE, will operate under the US Securities and Exchange Commission’s temporary Innovation Exemption and offer eligible US customers round-the-clock trading. Under the exemption, venues must give companies a chance to object before listing shares tokenized by an unaffiliated third party. JPMorgan Chase, McDonald’s, SpaceX and Coca-Cola were among the companies that objected. 

Tokenized stocks are blockchain-based tokens that represent company shares or track their price. The rights they carry depend on how they are structured. The distributed value of tokenized stocks and ETFs reached $3.88 billion on Nov. 11, up 13.4% over 30 days. 

In comments to Cointelegraph, former New York governor and OKXICE co-chair Andrew Cuomo said investors would have “the same rights, protections and ownership that come with the underlying shares.” 

OKX expects the venue to list more than 70 assets, including 59 exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and tokenized shares of Coinbase, Circle, BitGo, Robinhood and Strategy. The lineup also includes Strategy’s preferred shares.

Related: Public companies object to OKX-ICE’s tokenized stock plan

Tokenized stock trading raises liquidity concerns

The rollout comes amid concerns that trading the same shares across traditional exchanges and blockchain platforms could split liquidity and make prices less reliable. 

In October, a study by the International Monetary Fund found that the tokenized stocks were about 1.5 times as volatile as the same stocks in traditional markets. Decentralized exchanges had the weakest liquidity and their prices strayed further from those in traditional markets than prices on centralized exchanges did. 

The IMF also warned that combining trading and settlement on a blockchain could remove safeguards that help markets absorb shocks. As tokenized markets grow, greater use of leverage and closer links between markets could amplify fire sales, liquidity runs and financial contagion. 

Nasdaq argued in a January filing that trading tokenized stocks on platforms outside traditional rails could fragment liquidity and make it harder for investors to get the best available price. Regular US stock trading runs from 9:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. Eastern time on weekdays, excluding market holidays, though some brokers offer premarket, after-hours and overnight trading.

Cuomo described the current market structure was “built for another era,” arguing that crypto markets had already shown that trading could run around the clock. “Now we are bringing that standard to equities, without asking investors to settle for synthetic exposure or give up their shareholder rights,” he said.

title: Visa Adds Monad to Stablecoin Settlement Network
summary:
Key Takeaways: Visa has announced that Monad is becoming a new member of the Visa stablecoin settlement network for Monad’s issuers and acquirers. Visa’s stablecoin business currently amounts to more
The post Visa Adds Monad to Stablecoin Settlement Network appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Visa has announced that Monad is becoming a new member of the Visa stablecoin settlement network for Monad’s issuers and acquirers.
  • Visa’s stablecoin business currently amounts to more than $25 billion annually.
  • The integration provides financial institutions with an additional choice when it comes to settling Visa transactions that may be outside of traditional banking hours.

Visa continues to grow its infrastructure of money on the blockchain with the addition of Monad as an institutional settlement blockchain.

Stablecoins on Monad can now be used to settle obligations between card issuers and acquirers, which will take the high-performance Layer 1 into Visa’s multi-chain settlement network.

  • Visa Adds Monad to Its Stablecoin Settlement Network
  • Stablecoin Settlement Run Rate Passes $25 Billion
    • Monad Adds Institutional Privacy Infrastructure

Visa Adds Monad to Its Stablecoin Settlement Network

The integration is not on the consumer checkout side, but rather at the back end of card payments.

🌐 @Visa is expanding stablecoin settlement to Monad

Participating issuers and acquirers can now settle Visa obligations in stablecoins on the Monad blockchain https://t.co/WLiY9H8Hic

— Monad (@monad) November 10, 2026

Cards are issued by issuers to customers, and the acquirers are responsible for merchant payment processing. Once the clearing takes place, the participating institutions can settle the amounts owed through Visa using stablecoins on Monad.

This enables yet another channel to bypass traditional banking hours, such as weekends and holidays, giving settlement money an alternative path.

The network is permissionless and has the speed and scalability needed for payment settlement, Monad Foundation said. No naming of issuers or acquirers was made who will use Monad first or which stablecoins will be supported.

Read More: MoneyGram Launches Stablecoin Card in Colombia, Bringing Crypto Payments to 60M Users

Stablecoin Settlement Run Rate Passes $25 Billion

There has been a rapid increase in Visa’s settlement activity of stablecoins in 2026. Visa had earlier said in September it had reached a run rate of more than $20 billion annually.

By late October, Visa CEO Ryan McInerney said the annualized tally was higher than $25 billion, about 10 times the level a year ago. This is Visa’s total stablecoin settlement volume, across all its settlement networks, not necessarily volume settled via Monad.

In April, Visa rolled out its settlement testing initiative to nine blockchains and expanded the program to $7 billion per year.

Monad Adds Institutional Privacy Infrastructure

Monad’s Visa integration is part of its efforts to build privacy focused settlement infrastructure for financial institutions.

Monad’s proposed Private Settlement design would enable organizations to have execution environments with configurable validators, permissioned asset and access rules while keeping them connected to the main network.

Specific information such as sensitive transaction details and balances and contract state may not be available, and regulators or auditors may have access to specific information as needed. The privacy feature is not part of the existing Visa integration, but is still being developed. More privacy features are in the works in the near future, according to Monad Foundation.

By acquiring Monad, Visa is continuing an approach that has been in full swing over the last few weeks in which it has started to see stablecoins more as settlement utilities than just crypto assets. The network is providing the issuers and acquirers with additional ways to utilize blockchain and making Visa the shared layer that ties those settlement channels together.

title: LBank Faces $1M USDT Freeze Dispute After Trader Claims Profits Triggered Restrictions
summary:
Key Takeaways: LBank is accused of freezing around 1 million USDT after a trader profited from its futures trading and denied him opening positions, according to a Korean trader. LBank
The post LBank Faces $1M USDT Freeze Dispute After Trader Claims Profits Triggered Restrictions appeared first on C...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • LBank is accused of freezing around 1 million USDT after a trader profited from its futures trading and denied him opening positions, according to a Korean trader.
  • LBank says that profits are not the reason that an account gets restricted, and that they are reviewing accounts.
  • ZachXBT, a blockchain authorizer, derided coordinated-looking influencer posts supporting the exchange.

LBank, a leading crypto exchange, is under investigation for freezing about USD 1 million and halting futures trading after several successful trades.

LBank refuted the notion that the restrictions were caused by profits, stating that there is no reason, trading and withdrawals are normal, and they are in direct contact with the user.

Let’s clear this up 👇

We don’t restrict accounts just because someone makes a profit.

Trading and withdrawals are running normally. We’re working directly with the user on this account review and will share what we can while protecting their privacy.

If something isn’t right, tell us. Ask questions, share your experience and hold us accountable. That conversation belongs here, including criticism.

We’ll also defend ourselves against false claims. LBank has engaged external legal counsel to address false and misleading statements concerning this matter. The accompanying legal notice sets out our position.

Anyone who publishes or disseminates false and defamatory statements concerning this matter may face legal action. LBank will pursue appropriate legal remedies for any resulting damage to its reputation and legitimate interests.

To the media and creators covering this story: please check the facts before sharing, and correct anything inaccurate.

P.S. Nearly 100,000 of you trade futures on LBank every day. Let’s hear from you 👀

— LBank.com (@LBank_Exchange) November 10, 2026

  • Trader Says Restrictions Began After Profitable Futures Trading
  • LBank Says Account Review Is Ongoing
    • ZachXBT Criticizes LBank’s Public Defense

Trader Says Restrictions Began After Profitable Futures Trading

Apparently, the controversy started after the user, whose Twitter (X) handle is @solyflw34, engaged in the high-leverage futures game with large holdings of major cryptocurrencies including XRP, DOGE, XLM, NEAR, FIL and SUI.

🚨 LBank has frozen over $1M of my funds!

@LBank_Exchange @EH_LBank @xmuha0 @zachxbt @xiangzhang87 @ture_ath @Manjeet_LBank @Crypto__Haris

DO NOT USE THIS EXCHANGE

I made significant profits trading futures, and now my funds are frozen.

Here’s what happened 👇

1️⃣ Aug 31: I started making significant profits through high-leverage futures trading, primarily on major altcoins with relatively high market caps and trading volumes, including XRP, DOGE, XLM, NEAR, FIL, and SUI.

2️⃣ Sep 19: While withdrawing some of my funds as usual, my withdrawals were suddenly restricted without warning.

LBank requested additional verification and identity checks, and I completed all the required procedures and waited for their response.

3️⃣ Sep 29: LBank restricted trading on my futures positions and demanded a much more detailed explanation from me.

4️⃣ Oct 14: After weeks of waiting, I received their final response:

“The relevant abnormal funds will not be released.”

5️⃣ Current status: Since I was unable to close my futures positions due to the trading restrictions, they were eventually all liquidated as prices fell. Meanwhile, approximately 1M USDT remains frozen in my spot account.

I repeatedly asked LBank to explain:
• Which specific orders were considered abnormal?
• Which trades allegedly constituted market manipulation?
• Which accounts was I supposedly linked to?
• Exactly how much of my funds were classified as abnormal?
• Which specific clauses of their Terms of Service were being applied?
They have provided none of these details.

I was trading well-known assets such as NEAR, SUI, PEPE, BTC, FIL, LTC, SHIB, AVAX, ETH, and DOGE — not obscure, illiquid memecoins.

Yet my funds remain frozen without a clear explanation of what I allegedly did wrong.

Until this issue is resolved, I strongly urge everyone to reconsider using LBank.

If LBank continues to refuse to provide a transparent explanation or release my funds, I will continue raising awareness of this case within the Korean crypto community and bring it to the attention of relevant organizations, including Bithumb and DAXA.

I will keep pursuing this matter until I receive a fair resolution.

Users deserve transparency. Their funds should not be frozen without a clear and justified explanation.

@LBank_Exchange — I am still waiting for your response.

LBANK UID: LBA7H02780

For Korean (naver blog): https://t.co/HhLnZXj23n

— dlrrwad.edge🦭 (@solyfw34) November 10, 2026

The trader’s timeline says that the withdrawals have been discontinued since Sept. 19. LBank then asked to verify his ID and account, but he says that he filled those out as well.

On Sept. 29, the trader said futures trading was also restricted. This kept him from closing down jobs as they began to fall in price, according to him.

However, the user independently states that his spot account also has an amount of approximately 1 million USDT frozen and requests LBank to reveal exact trades, connected accounts and contractual clauses which underlie the reason.

Read More: Privacy Cash Freezes Deposits After $1.2M in Binance Hack Funds Hit Privacy Pools

LBank Says Account Review Is Ongoing

LBank said that unlike many other brokers, it doesn’t disqualify an account only for its profits. The exchange is currently in direct contact with the affected user and will share information it has with the user, while maintaining privacy. It also stated that it has also hired outside legal counsel with regards to any false or misleading statements.

The company threatened legal action over such accusations and urged the media and creators to confirm information before covering the incident.

The trader cannot agree with the description of the communication process by LBank, though, because he said he had already reached out to his account manager, their customer support, and the legal staff of the exchange prior to filing the dispute publicly.

ZachXBT Criticizes LBank’s Public Defense

Blockchain investigator ZachXBT also got in on the act, attacking some positive comments that came after LBank’s reply. He criticized the key Ops of the exchange for almost having the same messaging and called LBank an offshore centralized exchange that is unworthy to be engaged by serious traders.

@LBank_Exchange At least make it less obvious having your KOLs quote the post with the same script.

LBank is just another offshore bucket shop CEX no serious trader should ever touch. https://t.co/Qcfhns61tL

— ZachXBT (@zachxbt) November 10, 2026

The criticism now adds to the discussion but it still does not yield a definitive answer to the question of the moral permissibility of LBank’s account restrictions.

That is the crux of the matter: the trader argues his money was frozen for no good reason, and LBank states that the issue is being considered, but denies that profitable trading itself was the reason for restrictions.

title: Suiball Cancels Hardware Wallet Launch and Refunds Preorders in USDC After Security Review
summary:
Key Takeaways: Suiball is shutting down, yet its initial batch of hardware wallets has yet to reach its customers. Approximately 80% of the pre-orders were made onchain and a percentage
The post Suiball Cancels Hardware Wallet Launch and Refunds Preorders in USDC After Security Review appeared first...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Suiball is shutting down, yet its initial batch of hardware wallets has yet to reach its customers.
  • Approximately 80% of the pre-orders were made onchain and a percentage of these will receive a USDC refund.
  • According to the team, the Sui Foundation has recently suspended its backing of the project due to fear of attacks on the hardware wallets.

Despite being developed and starting to manufacture in this hardware wallet space, Sui-native hardware wallet project Suiball is literally shutting its doors.

The team said the decision followed a reassessment of hardware wallet risk by the Sui Foundation, leaving the project to close before shipping its first production batch.

Suiball Refund Announcement

Thank you to everyone who supported us on this journey.

We set out to build a secure hardware device that was more than just a hardware wallet: one fully native to Sui. We did it. Suiball went into manufacturing, and we were
ready to ship the first batch to our supporters.

After a wave of recent hardware wallet attacks across the industry, the Sui Foundation decided the risk of backing a hardware wallet project was too high right
now. We understand that decision. Sui puts the security of its users and ecosystem first.

Still, after years of intense development and a finished, working product, it’s hard to say that we have to close Suiball down. That’s the nature of building an ambitious startup. We had the right intentions and the right capabilities, but this one wasn’t meant to be.

How refunds work:

🔹 On-chain pre-orders (~80% of orders): You’ll get your refund in USDC, airdropped straight to the wallet that holds your soul bound pre-order NFT. You don’t
need to do anything. This will happen within the next week.

🔹 Credit card pre-orders: You’ll get an email asking for a Sui wallet address. Your refund will be airdropped there in USDC. We’ll run a second airdrop once addresses come in.

🔒 All the personal information you gave us for device delivery, including your name, email, shipping address, and phone number, will be permanently deleted once
refunds are complete. We won’t keep any records.

⚠ We will never ask for your seed phrase, private key, or any payment. Only reply to emails from [email protected]

Suiball will officially close once all refunds are complete. Thank you for believing in us.

— Suiball | Sui + Bitcoin Native (@suiballO) November 11, 2026

  • Suiball Ends Hardware Wallet Project Before First Shipment
  • Onchain Buyers Will Receive Automatic USDC Refunds
  • Customer Data Will Be Deleted After Refunds

Suiball Ends Hardware Wallet Project Before First Shipment

When it was made, Suiball said it already had a working device and had stepped up to manufacturing.

The team further revealed that, amidst some recent attacks by hardware wallets in the crypto industry, the Sui Foundation decided that launching the project was too risky to entrust clients at this time.

Suiball explained it knew of the decision, and that user security is the Foundation’s priority.

This closure was particularly significant as the product was far beyond the prototype phase. Suiball’s website featured a Sui-native device that offers native support for Sui transactions and move contracts, as well as Bitcoin support, NFC, bluetooth and secure element.

Read More: Sui’s Hashi Launches With $500M to Turn Bitcoin Into Productive DeFi Collateral Markets

Onchain Buyers Will Receive Automatic USDC Refunds

Refunds will depend on the way customers paid initially. Suiball estimated that 80% of pre-orders were done on-chain. Such a user will get USDC directly to the wallet where the user’s soulbound pre-order NFT is stored, without the need for any claims process.

The first refund, worth 400,000 Steller’s, will arrive within a week. The customers of the credit card will be getting an email instead now asking him/her to provide a Sui wallet address. Once those addresses are collected, Suiball will be refunding USDC as of a second round.

The team also alerted its customers that it will not ask them for seed phrases, private keys or extra payments during the procedure.

Customer Data Will Be Deleted After Refunds

Personal details used for device delivery purposes will be wiped after all the refunds are done, Suiball said. That means names, email addresses, shipping information, telephone numbers and so on. At the conclusion of the project, customer reimbursement will put the project out of service.

It follows a new and more conservative method of security Suiball had taken. The project previously held shipping up to allow for more audits instead of shipment now.

Its public product materials had positioned Suiball as the dedicated Sui wallet with touchscreens, EAL6+ secure element, Bluetooth, USB-C and NFC support.

Suiball’s pre-order site was still limited to cards and USDC, as the two refund methods are following suit at the moment to ease the strain on the project.

The team hasn’t claimed that there was a breach into the Suiball application, it said only that the third-party wallet app sustained the attack. The reasons it gives for closing are due to the larger risk assessment of any hardware wallet product and the disappearance of the Foundation’s backing.

title: MSCI Rules Today on Cutting Strategy (MSTR) From Its Indexes After a Draft List Marks It Deleted
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

MSCI Rules Today on Cutting Strategy (MSTR) From Its Indexes After a Draft List Marks It Deleted
MSCI publishes its November index review at 5 p.m. ET, the first under a new non-operating company screen. Its potential list, built on Sept. 30 filings, already marks Strategy, Metapla...
content:
MSCI will say Wednesday evening whether Strategy stays in its global stock indexes, after its own potential list already marked the largest corporate bitcoin holder as Deleted.

The index provider publishes its November 2026 Index Review shortly after 5 p.m. ET. MSCI said on Oct. 15 that the review would carry the final list of current constituents hit by the new screen, with any deletions taking effect at the close of Nov. 30.

MSCI’s list of potentially impacted securities, published with the Oct. 15 decision and built on Sept. 30 financial data and Oct. 9 market values, already marks five companies as Deleted: Strategy (MSTR), uranium holder Yellow Cake, Japan’s Metaplanet, Iceland’s Skel Fjárfestingafélag and micro-cap Upexi.

Strategy is the only large-cap name in the group and by float-adjusted market value accounts for more than 90% of the five. The company held 850,364 bitcoin as of Nov. 8, acquired at an average price of $75,456 a coin.

How the MSCI screen works

The rule does not mention bitcoin. MSCI first checks whether a company’s operating assets exceed 50% of total assets. Issuers that fail face five financial ratios, and a company flagged on four or more of them is ineligible for the MSCI Global Investable Market Indexes.

Buffers limit turnover. A company outside the indexes cannot be added if it fails the screen in either of its two most recent annual filing periods, but a current constituent is removed only if it fails in each of them. MSCI said it may also use the most recent interim filing.

That two-filing test is the question hanging over Strategy. It adopted fair-value accounting for its bitcoin at the start of 2025, so its fiscal 2024 statements carried the coins at cost less impairment, and MSCI has not said how it treats that earlier year. A Deleted mark implies MSCI’s draft reading is that Strategy already failed both periods, but it has not published the inputs behind that placement.

Strategy has argued that it reports its bitcoin treasury as an operating segment and books related gains and losses in operating expenses.

The screen replaces an approach aimed squarely at crypto. MSCI first proposed in late 2025 to exclude companies whose digital assets made up 50% or more of total assets, then dropped that plan in January and opened a broader consultation in August. The new rule also ends the interim measures MSCI placed on those companies in October 2025, including a freeze on share-count increases and a deferral of additions.

What a deletion would and would not do

Funds that track an MSCI index have to hold what the index holds, so a deletion would force them to sell by the Nov. 30 close. JPMorgan analysts estimated last November that an MSCI exclusion could drive about $2.8 billion of outflows from Strategy, and as much as $8.8 billion more if other index providers followed. That estimate was built on MSCI’s earlier digital-asset proposal, not the October screen, and MSCI itself has published no figure.

A removal would not delist Strategy’s stock, and nothing in the rules forces the company to sell bitcoin. The pressure would land on the shares, and through them on the premium Strategy uses to fund new purchases by selling stock. In an August letter to MSCI, the company said a deletion “would have no meaningful impact on Strategy’s business.”

Strategy’s own cushion is already thin. It bought 1,036 bitcoin for $81.9 million in the week to Nov. 8, a purchase that left its holdings below that average cost. Bitcoin traded near $73,900 Wednesday.

If Strategy fails only its latest filing rather than both, it would not be deleted this round and would instead go on a watchlist. The potential list already places 17 other constituents there, including SharpLink, TON Strategy and Solana Company.

Tokyo-listed Metaplanet faces the same Deleted mark, after it sold bitcoin last quarter to show investors it could tap its holdings for liquidity. The test now is whether Wednesday’s official list sticks with those Deleted marks, or whether MSCI pulls any of the five back onto the watchlist.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Telegram’s Gram Wallets Pass 1 million in 48 Hours, GRAM Price Climbs 10.23%
summary:
Key Takeaways: In the first 48 hours, over 1 million self-custodial Gram wallets have been activated on Telegram. According to a screen grab, there were 1,008,151 activations and the latest
The post Telegram’s Gram Wallets Pass 1 million in 48 Hours, GRAM Price Climbs 10.23% appeared first on Crypto...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • In the first 48 hours, over 1 million self-custodial Gram wallets have been activated on Telegram.
  • According to a screen grab, there were 1,008,151 activations and the latest wallet appeared four minutes ago.
  • GRAM has a displayed market cap of $3.39 billion and currently sits at $1.18, -up 10.23% in 24 hours.

Telegram’s crypto ecosystem has just reached a milestone of adoption; sharing has seen over one million self-custodial Gram wallets activated within two days of the launch. Pavel Durov, the Telegram founder, released the news in parallel with a sudden surge in the price of GRAM, which made it one of the best-on-trading tokens on the crypto market.

  • Telegram Records Over 1 million Gram Wallet Activations
    • GRAM Price Rises 10.23% in 24 Hours
  • Wallet Activations Do Not Equal Active Users
    • Telegram Expands Its Crypto Ecosystem

Telegram Records Over 1 million Gram Wallet Activations

Durov shared this news on November 11 indicating over a million self-custodial Gram wallets had been activated within 48 hours.

1M+ self-custodial Gram wallets activated on Telegram in just 48 hours.

$GRAM is up 10% in 24h, the #1 gainer in the CMC top 100. https://t.co/VGVTT5AZQk

— Pavel Durov (@durov) November 11, 2026

The image attached gives a more accurate number of 1008151 activations in this timeframe. It also indicated that the latest wallet activation on the record was approximately 4 minutes prior to the image capture, presumably meaning that new wallets had been activated since then too.

The swift expansion underscores Telegram’s capability to seamlessly bring the crypto money sector straight to its messaging environment. Users do not need to use different platforms or applications to access the wallet services but can utilize them within a user-friendly application.

The aspect that is relevant here is the self-custodial feature, which ensures that users have direct control over their crypto wallets; avoiding a third-party service with the control of the assets.

Read More: Binance Flags iOS Flaw That Could Expose iPhone Users’ Crypto Wallets and Private Keys

GRAM Price Rises 10.23% in 24 Hours

The wallet milestone complemented with good market performance of GRAM. The token rose by 10% over a period of 24 hours and went to the top five of CoinMarketCap’s top 100 cryptocurrencies, said Durov. The image displayed is of GRAM at $1.18, with a 24-hour rise of 10.23%. It also had a market cap of nearly $3.39 billion.

These numbers highlight the token’s price performance as it continues to see an expansion in wallet activations. Those two indicators are related to adoption differently, though: wallet activations are registrations or activations, while price movements relate to market trading figures.

Wallet Activations Do Not Equal Active Users

Each of them reaches one million activations, but not necessarily if every wallet is actively holding or transferring GRAM. Transaction counts, active addresses, and repeat usage would provide a clearer picture of sustained activity.

Telegram Expands Its Crypto Ecosystem

The new stats help highlight how Telegram is increasingly becoming a service that contains crypto wallet functions. An incorporation of self-custodial wallets and a regulated application might alleviate the hurdles to the entry of customers who wish to explore the digital assets.

One million activations of the wallet in 48 hours and 10.23% an average daily gain are great events for GRAM. Whether this growth will lead to some degree of consistent hosting has got to be one of the metrics to consider.

title: Tether’s 800M AI Agent Outperforms Models 2.5 Times Its Size in Six Tool-Use Tests
summary:
Key Takeaways: Tether’s QVAC BotPsy-0.8B beat models with up to 2.5 times more parameters in six agentic tests. The tool-use score of the 800M-parameter model almost doubled the scores of
The post Tether’s 800M AI Agent Outperforms Models 2.5 Times Its Size in Six Tool-Use Tests appeared first on Cr...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Tether’s QVAC BotPsy-0.8B beat models with up to 2.5 times more parameters in six agentic tests.
  • The tool-use score of the 800M-parameter model almost doubled the scores of its base Qwen3.5-0.8B-Think architecture.
  • To move more powerful AI assistants to personal devices and put them away from centralized servers, Tether plans to do so.

Tether has introduced QVAC BotPsy, an open-weight AI model designed to execute tasks through apps and external tools. The model, with only 0.8 billion parameters, beat bigger models on tests arranged by Tether, suggesting the ability of tailored AI to serve daily needs on individual gadgets.

Tether’s 800M AI Agent Beats Models 2.5x Its Size on Everyday Phone Tasks
Learn more: https://t.co/3GFAZrkM9W

— Tether (@tether) November 11, 2026

  • Tether’s 800M Model Challenges Larger AI Systems
  • BotPsy Turns Everyday Requests into Actions
    • Local AI Could Reduce Reliance on Centralized Servers

Tether’s 800M Model Challenges Larger AI Systems

After the announcement on November 11, QVAC BotPsy outperformed all models with 1.2 billion or fewer parameters on six respective agentic benchmarks: BFCL v4, ACEBench, τ-bench, Claw-Eval, BrowseComp-Plus, and ToolSandbox.

On four key metrics, BotPsy almost doubled the scores given by its base model Qwen3.5-0.8B-Think. It improved its score for BWFC v4 from 23.4 to 44.0 and ACEBench from 30.1 to 58.7. It also raised its scores on the τ-bench and ToolSandbox benchmarks up to 51.5 and 64.6, respectively.

Tether also claims that BotPsy does outperform Alibaba’s model Qwen3.5-2B-Think, which has 2.5 times the number of parameters. The base model achieved 46.1 points and the larger model 23.8 points on BFCL multi-turn tool calling, whereas its base architecture got 7.5 points.

BotPsy significantly outpaced MiniCPM5-1B-Think with a score of 82.5, outshone Qwen3.5-2B-Think with 69.3 and edged out LLama3-3B-Think at 74.4.

Read More: Tether Q3 Profit Hits $1.5B While USDT Reserve Buffer Nearly Doubles to $8B

BotPsy Turns Everyday Requests into Actions

BotPy is not built for generation of responses only like AI models are, but it is built to call the right tool calls in multiple steps. This might help with organizing activities, sending messages, and even travel arrangements.

One ACEBench test attempted to send a message, but it was unable to do so due to a lack of Wi-Fi connectivity and a full inbox. BotPsy spotted both, activated WiFi, removed inbox space and then sent the message. Instead, its bottom line will try the same action repeatedly that it has failed on.

The model can define when there may be no available tool needed to address a request as opposed to making an unwanted Call. This is significant for assistants that must perform numerous actions and modify content.

Local AI Could Reduce Reliance on Centralized Servers

BotPsy is based on Alibaba’s open-source Qwen3.5 and is sufficiently small to allow it to be explored on personal hardware. Requests could be satisfied locally, limiting the amount of sensitive information: emails, contacts, calendars, and more, sent to central providers.

CEO Paolo Ardoino noted that with local AI, users will have more control over the processing of their personal data and the accessibility of services for their assistant.

BotPsy extends the QVAC ecosystem developed by Tether including VisionPsy which tackles Visual Question Answering, TranscribePsy which addresses speech and TranslatePsy which addresses translation tasks, etc.
