title: Crypto News Today: Santiment Data Shows Extreme Fear in BTC, ETH, and XRP With $2.15B in Bitcoin ETF Outflows
summary: Crypto market sentiment has deteriorated across Bitcoin, Ethereum, and XRP, while sustained withdrawals from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs highlight growing investor caution.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC ETH XRP

Crypto market sentiment has deteriorated across Bitcoin, Ethereum, and XRP, while sustained withdrawals from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs highlight growing investor caution.

Santiment’s latest social data shows bearish commentary outweighing bullish discussions across all three cryptocurrencies. Meanwhile, approximately $2.15 billion in net Bitcoin ETF outflows since October 30 has added to concerns as Bitcoin tests the $73,000 price region.

Santiment Data Shows Extreme Fear Across BTC, ETH, and XRP

Social sentiment surrounding Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), and XRP has fallen into bearish territory, according to Santiment’s latest analysis of discussions across X, Reddit, Telegram, and other social platforms.

The data shows BTC recording a positive-to-negative comment ratio of 0.82, while ETH stands at 0.88. XRP registered the weakest reading at 0.49, indicating considerably more negative than positive commentary. A reading below 1.0 means bearish comments outnumber bullish ones.

Bitcoin, Ethereum, and XRP sentiment has fallen deep into bearish territory. Source: @SantimentData/X

These figures suggest that pessimism has spread across different segments of the cryptocurrency market. XRP’s reading is particularly weak, with fewer than one positive comment for every two negative comments. Bitcoin and Ethereum are also experiencing negative sentiment despite their relatively higher ratios.

Santiment highlighted the development in a November 10 post on X, describing the situation as a point where “Retail Fear is Reaching a BOILING POINT.” The analytics firm noted that traders have become increasingly pessimistic as cryptocurrency prices approach recent lows.

However, social sentiment readings should not be confused with actual investor positioning. The ratios measure the balance of positive and negative discussions rather than the amount of cryptocurrency investors hold or the volume of assets they have sold.

Bitcoin ETF Outflows Reach $2.15 Billion

Adding to the negative market backdrop, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have experienced substantial withdrawals. Santiment Data reported approximately $2.15 billion in cumulative net outflows since October 30, reflecting a shift in investor activity during Bitcoin’s recent decline.

Daily ETF flow figures show the pressure building across several trading sessions. On October 30, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $643.2 million in net outflows. The withdrawals continued in November, with another $398.6 million leaving the funds on November 2 and $430.2 million on November 5.

Heavy ETF selling can become a valuable counter-signal when fear reaches an extreme. Source: @SantimentData/X

The trend continued on November 6, when the ETFs recorded approximately $411.9 million in additional net outflows. A further $201 million exited the products on November 9.

The latest reported session added another $95 million in withdrawals on November 10. Consequently, finalized daily flow figures from October 30 through November 10 indicate cumulative net outflows of approximately $2.22 billion, slightly above the $2.15 billion figure reported in the earlier snapshot.

This development coincides with Bitcoin’s renewed weakness, as the asset slipped below $74,000 and approached the $73,000 area. The combination of falling prices and sustained ETF withdrawals points to a defensive shift among investors.

Spot Bitcoin ETF flows provide an indication of demand for regulated Bitcoin investment products. However, the figures do not identify whether withdrawals came from retail investors, institutional investors, or both. They also represent only one segment of the broader cryptocurrency market.

Extreme Pessimism Could Present a Contrarian Signal

Despite the negative readings, Santiment’s analysis highlights a different interpretation of the current market environment. Historically, periods of widespread pessimism have sometimes appeared before significant cryptocurrency recoveries.

The reasoning behind this contrarian view is that market rallies do not necessarily begin when investors are optimistic. In some cases, prices begin recovering when selling pressure has intensified, confidence has weakened, and much of the short-term buying interest has disappeared.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

When negative sentiment becomes widespread, expectations may already reflect substantial downside concerns. This can leave less room for additional selling if market conditions begin to stabilize.

The current readings across BTC, ETH, and XRP therefore offer a potential contrarian signal. Bitcoin’s 0.82 ratio, Ethereum’s 0.88 reading, and XRP’s 0.49 level show that bearish commentary currently dominates discussions surrounding these assets.

However, extreme fear alone does not establish that a market bottom is in place. Negative sentiment can persist during prolonged declines, while continued ETF withdrawals may indicate that demand has yet to recover.

The relationship between sentiment and price action will therefore remain important. A meaningful change in investor behavior would require more than a temporary improvement in social commentary.

What Investors Will Watch Next

The coming trading sessions could provide further insight into whether the current pessimism represents a late-stage selling environment or the beginning of another period of market weakness.

For Bitcoin, the ability to stabilize around the $73,000 region and recover lost ground will remain an important market reference. Continued ETF withdrawals would indicate that demand for spot Bitcoin investment products remains under pressure.

Sentiment readings for Ethereum and XRP will also be worth monitoring. A sustained recovery toward or above the neutral 1.0 threshold would indicate that positive discussions are becoming more competitive with bearish commentary.

ETF flow reversals could provide another indication of changing investor behavior. A return to consistent net inflows, combined with improving social sentiment and price stability, would offer stronger evidence that market confidence is recovering.

For now, Santiment’s data presents a market characterized by widespread fear, while Bitcoin ETF withdrawals highlight continued caution across investment products. Although both developments can appear near market turning points, neither confirms that the latest cryptocurrency decline has ended.

title: Glassnode Flags 7.12 Million Bitcoin With Exposed Public Keys: What Quantum Risk Means
summary: Bitcoin quantum risk data puts 35.4% of supply behind visible public keys. What Glassnode measured, why address reuse matters and what remains unproven.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Bitcoin quantum risk data puts 35.4% of supply behind visible public keys. What Glassnode measured, why address reuse matters and what remains unproven.

Bitcoin quantum risk is back in focus after Glassnode reported that 7.12 million BTC, or 35.4% of issued supply, sits behind public keys already visible on-chain. The number is striking. What it measures is more specific than a claim that a third of Bitcoin has been hacked or can be stolen with today’s machines.

The fresh November 10 data puts a measurable scale on a future cryptographic concern. It also highlights a practical difference between exposure built into an address type and exposure created by how wallets reuse addresses.

What Glassnode’s new Bitcoin figures show

In its November 10 update, Glassnode said 25.8% of supply was exposed through address reuse, including 11.6% on exchanges. The exchange figure sits within the reuse category. Adding those percentages together would double-count coins.

“Moving those coins to a fresh address ends this exposure,” the firm wrote, referring to the reuse-related problem. That statement is not a guarantee that any new address format protects against every future quantum attack.

Glassnode’s original methodology, published in May, put visible-key exposure at 30.2% of issued supply, or 6.04 million BTC. The November reading is 5.2 percentage points higher. That comparison describes a change in measured exposure, not a demonstrated increase in the capabilities of quantum computers.

A public key is not a stolen private key

A private key authorises a Bitcoin transaction. Its corresponding public key lets the network verify a signature. Under the cryptographic assumptions used today, knowing a public key does not make deriving its private key computationally practical.

The concern is a sufficiently capable quantum computer applying a different mathematical approach to recover private keys from public keys. Glassnode’s framework asks which coins already have the necessary public information visible while they remain unspent.

Its methodology calls this exposure at rest. That is different from a public key becoming visible when the owner broadcasts a spending transaction. The latter creates a shorter window in which an attacker would have to act.

The distinction explains why a large exposed balance does not establish an attack timeline. A map of potential targets and proof of a machine able to attack them are different kinds of evidence. The latest dataset supplies the former, not the latter.

Address reuse is the operational issue

Glassnode separates structural exposure from operational exposure. Some output types reveal keys by design; others can conceal them until spending. Reusing a key after it has been revealed can leave remaining or future funds associated with information already recorded on the blockchain.

For a custodian, that makes the topic partly about wallet management. An organisation can have strong controls against password theft and unauthorised withdrawals while still wanting a separate inventory of which outputs have visible public keys.

Those controls address different threats. A public-key exposure metric should not be used on its own to declare an exchange insolvent, compromised or unsafe in every respect. Nor should a low measured exposure be treated as a complete security audit.

The useful question for a service provider is whether it understands its address types and transaction history, and can explain how it plans to manage future cryptographic changes. This is a more concrete discussion than asking whether a company is simply for or against quantum preparedness.

Bitcoin’s proposed response is still a proposal

One approach appears in BIP 360, a draft Bitcoin Improvement Proposal for Pay-to-Merkle-Root outputs. It aims to reduce long-duration public-key exposure while preserving script-tree functionality. It is not an activated network upgrade.

The authors separate long-exposure attacks from faster attacks attempted while a transaction waits for confirmation. They say fuller protection against the latter may require post-quantum signatures. A mechanism that hides a public key for longer should therefore not be described as a complete replacement for quantum-resistant signing.

That distinction matters when evaluating claims that Bitcoin has already fixed the problem. Publishing a proposal is one step. Reviewing the design, reaching agreement, implementing it and persuading holders to use any eventual change are separate challenges.

The draft itself acknowledges uncertainty about when or whether cryptographically relevant quantum computers will become viable. It offers a possible way to prepare without providing a countdown to a proven attack.

Why this is a governance question too

Changes affecting widely held digital money involve coordination as well as cryptography. Wallet developers, custodians and holders need compatible tools and clear information. Dormant holdings raise additional questions because an inactive owner cannot be assumed to participate in a future migration.

BNC’s coverage of Strategy’s Bitcoin treasury and capital allocation shows how material BTC balances have become for corporate investors. For such holders, long-term custody planning belongs alongside financing and asset-management decisions.

The new Glassnode figures give that planning a more precise starting point. They identify a large stock of coins with visible keys and show why address reuse deserves attention. They do not establish that those coins have been stolen, that an attack is imminent or that Bitcoin’s price must move in a particular direction.

The next meaningful evidence would be improved exposure reporting, progress on reviewed technical proposals and independently demonstrated advances in relevant quantum capabilities. Until then, the strongest interpretation is preparedness: a clearer map of the potential problem, with substantial work still ahead.

title: Russia’s Central Bank Clears Exchange to Open Bitcoin and Crypto Trading on Nov. 22
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Russia’s Central Bank Clears Exchange to Open Bitcoin and Crypto Trading on Nov. 22
A Bank of Russia ordinance published Wednesday lets exchanges start organized crypto trading on Nov. 22, but only after the central bank approves their rules. Moscow Exchange still aims for Dec. 1.
...
content:
The Bank of Russia said Wednesday that exchanges may start organized trading in cryptocurrencies on Nov. 22, once the central bank has approved their trading rules, a step that lands just ahead of Moscow Exchange’s planned Dec. 1 bitcoin launch.

The ordinance, which amends the Bank of Russia’s rules for organized trading, was registered by the Justice Ministry on Nov. 3 and published Wednesday on the regulator’s site. It takes effect 10 days after publication, on Nov. 22.

Exchanges will have to register the brokers, trust managers and central counterparties that take part in crypto trades, keep registers of orders and deals, and monitor the activity. They must also calculate a current price, a weighted-average price, a market price and a closing price, and report trading activity to the central bank in the same way they already do for other assets.

The regulator was clear about the order of operations. Exchanges may open crypto markets from Nov. 22, it said, “but first they must agree with the regulator on the rules for conducting such trading.” It did not say whether any venue has already cleared that review.

Who can buy, and what they can buy

A separate ordinance, published Nov. 6 and due to take effect Nov. 17, sets the menu for ordinary buyers. The Bank of Russia approved bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT for purchase by non-qualified investors, and said exchanges may admit those assets to public trading from that date.

Non-qualified investors can buy through a broker, a trust manager or a registered crypto exchange office, on an exchange or over the counter. Purchases through a single intermediary may not exceed 300,000 rubles a year, roughly $3,600 at the official exchange rate. Qualified investors can access all cryptoassets with no purchase cap.

Both groups still have to pass a knowledge test and read a risk disclosure before they can trade. The list is limited to the most liquid assets that meet the law’s tests for market capitalization, average daily volume and at least five years of pricing history on foreign exchanges.

Moscow Exchange still aims for Dec. 1

Moscow Exchange, Russia’s largest trading venue, announced on Nov. 2 that it plans to offer bitcoin, ether and USDT trades from Dec. 1, initially as a pilot while participants connect. Trading would run on its existing stock-market systems from 6:50 a.m. to 11:50 p.m. Moscow time, with the National Clearing Centre clearing the deals and clients able to settle the same day or the next.

Bitcoin Magazine reported the Dec. 1 plan last week, including the U.S. sanctions that already cover the exchange and its clearing house. Boris Blokhin, a senior managing director at the exchange, said in early October that Moscow Exchange would not need additional licenses to start and would use a partner settlement digital depository. Wednesday’s notice still requires the central bank to sign off on the trading rules themselves. The exchange has not said publicly whether that approval is already in hand.

SPB Exchange, the St. Petersburg venue, has said it wants to start organized crypto trading by the end of the year and is building a settlement digital depository of its own, Russian newspaper Vedomosti reported in October.

The market sits on Federal Law No. 282-FZ, “On Digital Currencies and Digital Rights,” whose main provisions took effect on Sept. 1. The law licenses exchanges, brokers, managers, depositories and exchangers, recognizes crypto as property and opens a supervised channel for cross-border trade. It still bans using crypto to pay for goods and services inside Russia. Officials have spent the fall standing up the rest of the plumbing, including a self-regulatory body for crypto exchanges and digital depositories.

The test now is not whether Russia will have a legal exchange market for bitcoin, but when the first venue actually opens, and whether a 300,000-ruble retail cap is enough to pull traders off the offshore desks they already use.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: ICE and OKX Set Nov. 23 Tokenized Stock Launch After 67 Companies Opt Out
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

ICE and OKX Set Nov. 23 Tokenized Stock Launch After 67 Companies Opt Out
The joint venture will offer more than 70 assets, including tokenized shares of Strategy, Coinbase and Circle plus 59 Direxion ETFs, even after Tesla, Apple, Meta and Netflix objected.
This post ICE and OKX S...
content:
OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) will open their tokenized stock venue on Nov. 23, the companies said Wednesday, offering more than 70 assets under a temporary SEC exemption even as 67 companies, including Apple, Tesla and Meta, have already objected.

The OKX announcement said more than 70 assets are expected to be listed, including securities from Better.com, BitGo, Circle, Coinbase, Robinhood, Securitize and Strategy (MSTR), as well as 59 exchange-traded funds from Direxion. Strategy will also list its preferred stocks, such as STRC.

Access at launch is limited to eligible U.S. customers of OKX Inc. who have activated a CeDeFi Wallet, passed identity checks and completed onboarding with the joint venture, which is called OKXICE and is owned equally by ICE and OKC USA Holding Inc., an OKX affiliate. Trading will run around the clock in the OKX app.

“The future of finance is onchain, and we have an opportunity to build it here in America, with the standards, safeguards and ambition that investors expect,” said former New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo, who co-chairs OKXICE with Trabue Bland.

The companies did not say how many of the more than 70 assets will trade on the first day, or how much liquidity the pools will have at the open. The venue is not a registered exchange or broker-dealer and is not approved by the SEC, the announcement said.

How the venue will work

Trading will run through automated market maker pools built on Uniswap v4 and deployed on X Layer, the Ethereum layer-2 network OKX operates. Only approved wallets can trade or add liquidity.

Securitize will provide the tokenization infrastructure. Each token represents a security entitlement backed one-for-one by a U.S. share held by a registered broker-dealer, and holders keep the usual shareholder rights, including dividends, voting and corporate actions, the venue said in a Nov. 5 public notice required under the exemption.

Customers will hold the tokens in their own wallets. OKXICE will not hold the assets or the private keys. The tokens will be paired with payment stablecoins such as USDC and USDG. The venue does not operate an order book, does not extend credit and does not conduct primary offerings, the notice said.

67 companies have already opted out

The same Nov. 5 notice lists 67 issuers that had sent a written objection by that date, among them Apple, Amazon, Tesla, Meta, Netflix, Nvidia, Microsoft, JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Costco, Nike and Home Depot. The list has grown from 50 objectors in an Oct. 30 notice.

The objections stem from the SEC’s five-year “Innovation Exemption,” issued Sept. 17, which lets tokenized securities venues trade blockchain versions of U.S. stocks through automated market makers without registering as exchanges. When an unaffiliated third party tokenizes a company’s stock, the venue must notify the issuer, which then has 30 days to object in writing.

The SEC’s innovation exemption page lists OKXICE TSV as having submitted a notice of intent on Oct. 4.

The names the companies highlighted are mostly crypto-linked. Strategy, the largest public bitcoin treasury company, is listing both its common stock and its preferreds. “Tokenization on the OKXICE TSV is a natural next step toward making Digital Credit accessible to investors around the world, 24 hours a day, seven days a week,” Strategy’s president and chief executive, Phong Le, said in the announcement, referring to preferreds such as STRC. Le also called bitcoin “Digital Capital.”

The test now is whether a venue that has lost Apple, Tesla, Nvidia and most of the rest of the largest U.S. companies can still draw enough trading to matter when it opens in 12 days, and whether any more issuers object before then.

For context, a tokenized stock is a blockchain token backed one-for-one by a real share. Under the SEC’s Innovation Exemption, the venue can list these tokens without the issuing company’s consent, unless the company objects within 30 days.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Former Cointelegraph CEO Joins Phase as Co-Founder and CEO
summary: The appointment follows the launch of Phase’s Layer 1 blockchain mainnet and AI agent services, backed by $45 million in founder funding. content:
The appointment follows the launch of Phase’s Layer 1 blockchain mainnet and AI agent services, backed by $45 million in founder funding.

SAN FRANCISCO, November 11, 2026 — Phase, a technology company building the operating layer for the AI agent economy, today announced that Yana Prikhodchenko, former CEO of Cointelegraph, has joined the company as co-founder and CEO. She will lead strategy, global expansion and commercial development, working alongside founder Kirill Eves, as Phase scales its decentralized infrastructure for autonomous AI agents.

Prikhodchenko joins Phase after nearly five years at Cointelegraph, where she served as CEO, leading a global team of more than 200 people and transforming the company from a crypto news platform into a diversified group spanning media, marketing, research, acceleration and industry events. Before joining Cointelegraph, she spent more than a decade in senior leadership roles at major banking and insurance companies, including Allianz.

Phase is building the operating layer for the AI agent economy, giving AI agents everything they need to operate autonomously, from accessing the open web and orchestrating AI models to performing computing tasks and making payments. These services run on Phase’s Layer 1 blockchain, powered by a decentralized network of everyday devices whose owners earn rewards for validating transactions and contributing connectivity and computing power.

“AI agents are moving from answering questions to performing real tasks on our behalf, but the infrastructure they depend on was not built for autonomous systems. Phase is building an open, decentralized network that anyone can participate in. My focus is to bring this technology to developers and businesses worldwide and build the ecosystem needed to support the next generation of AI agents,” said Yana Prikhodchenko, co-founder and CEO of Phase.

“Yana brings extensive leadership experience across media, technology and financial services, along with the operational expertise and industry relationships needed to take Phase into its next stage of growth. As we bring our technology to market, she will lead the company’s commercial development and global expansion,” said Kirill Eves, founder of Phase.

About Phase

Phase is a technology company building the operating layer for the AI agent economy, with four integrated services that give AI agents everything they need to operate autonomously, from accessing the open web and orchestrating AI models to performing computing tasks and making payments. The platform runs on its own Layer 1 blockchain, powered by a decentralized network of everyday devices. Phase has received $45 million in funding from its founder, Kirill Eves.

Phase Proxy enables AI agents acting on behalf of users to access websites that restrict automated traffic through mobile and residential internet connections. Phase Router intelligently directs requests across leading AI models to optimize quality, performance and cost. Phase Compute harnesses the processing power of devices across the network to run open-weight AI models, while on-chain settlement enables autonomous payments using stablecoins and PHASE, the network’s native token. Phase is building its own AI model to serve as the platform’s central intelligence, capable of advanced reasoning, solving complex tasks independently and orchestrating other AI models.

Unlike most blockchain networks that require dedicated servers or token staking, Phase allows anyone to become a validator simply by downloading the app, without specialized hardware or upfront investment. Its reputation-based consensus and randomized validator selection secure the network and prevent control from concentrating in the hands of a few powerful operators. Phase rewards device owners with PHASE tokens for validating blocks and contributing connectivity and computing power, enabling millions of people to help build the AI economy and share in the value it creates.

For more information, visit phase.xyz.

title: ARK Invest Trims Block and Bullish Positions as Bitcoin ETF Outflows Continue
summary: Disclosed ARK Invest trading activity points to sales of shares in crypto-linked companies Block and Bullish alongside changes elsewhere in its…
content:
TL;DR: Disclosed ARK Invest trading activity points to sales of shares in crypto-linked companies Block and Bullish alongside changes elsewhere in its portfolios. A fund manager selling shares is not the same as investors redeeming money from a spot Bitcoin ETF, and the trades should not be treated as a categorical forecast for crypto prices.

Crypto markets generate several types of selling headlines, but they do not all describe the same thing. One involves investors moving money into or out of exchange-traded products. Another involves a fund manager changing which companies it owns inside a portfolio. ARK Invest’s latest trade disclosures belong to the second category.

ARK’s trade-notification service provides information about purchases and sales by its exchange-traded funds. Reporting of the November 9 trades indicates reductions in shares of Block and Bullish, both businesses tied to the wider digital-asset economy.

Trade data published for the session should be checked against the original ARK notification for exact fund allocations and amounts. Public summaries can combine activity across several ETFs, while dollar-value estimates change with the share price used for calculation.

Why a portfolio trade is not a market-wide verdict

A growth-oriented fund might sell shares to rebalance position weights, manage liquidity, fund purchases of other holdings or respond to company-specific developments. A share sale alone cannot reveal which of those motives dominated.

For that reason, it would be a mistake to describe ARK’s selling as proof that the manager has abandoned Bitcoin. The sale may reflect a view on the risk and valuation of individual equities rather than the future value of the underlying cryptocurrency.

Block’s exposure to digital assets is also different from Bullish’s. Their revenue drivers, regulation and business models are not interchangeable merely because both are routinely grouped under the label ‘crypto stock.’ Investors comparing them need to look beyond the common theme.

ETF redemptions tell a different story

NewsBTC has recently tracked sizable outflows from US spot Bitcoin funds and earlier daily Bitcoin ETF withdrawals. Those figures measure net investor flows into or out of specific products, rather than an ETF manager switching between equity holdings.

Even within ETF reporting, transactions can be misunderstood. Selling shares in a listed company held by an actively managed ETF does not necessarily imply the ETF itself suffered a redemption. Likewise, a Bitcoin ETF net outflow does not automatically show why an individual investor chose to redeem.

Those distinctions become especially important in a market where the same financial firm may own Bitcoin directly, operate a fund holding mining or exchange equities, and manage entirely different technology-sector positions.

The wider context for crypto-linked shares

Shares of trading venues, payment companies and miners are often affected by crypto prices but can also move on earnings results, borrowing costs and capital spending. A mining company pursuing AI infrastructure may be valued on its power contracts as much as its Bitcoin output. A brokerage might add accounts while earning less from crypto transactions.

That mixture means crypto-equity portfolio changes sometimes convey a different message from spot-token trading activity. They are better read as part of ongoing active management than as standalone signals to buy or sell a coin.

What the disclosures can establish

The strongest verifiable facts are the securities traded, the direction of the trade and the number of shares reported for each fund. If later reporting establishes exact price-weighted values, those should be dated and described as estimates where appropriate.

ARK’s trading notices offer a window into portfolio decisions, not a complete explanation of motive. Their value for readers comes from knowing precisely what changed and avoiding the temptation to translate every share sale into a broad claim about the Bitcoin market.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

summary:

Disclaimer

  • Finance Magnates and iSAM Securities will host a free webinar on 1 December 2026, exploring broker P&L losses, negative balance protection abuse, cross-broker hedging and the challenges of identifying trading risks through conventional monitoring.

Where are brokers losing money, and why can certain trading activities go undetected even when individual accounts appear legitimate?

Finance Magnates and iSAM Securities are hosting a free webinar on 1 December 2026 at 2:00 PM Cyprus Time, examining the trading strategies and client behaviours that can affect broker profitability. Dennis Weissert, Chief Commercial Officer (CCO) at iSAM Securities, will examine the challenges of broker risk management, including how negative balance protection abuse, swap and bonus exploitation, and cross-broker hedging can affect profitability.

Where Broker P&L Losses Can Go Unnoticed

Broker profitability is influenced by more than trading volumes and market conditions. Certain trading behaviours can create financial exposure that may be difficult to identify through conventional monitoring.

Negative balance protection abuse, swap and bonus exploitation, and cross-broker hedging are among the activities that can affect a broker's bottom line. Although individual accounts may appear legitimate when reviewed separately, the broader trading activity can reveal risks that are less obvious at account level.

According to iSAM Securities, 1% of clients can account for 30% of a broker's total drawdown, highlighting how losses may be concentrated among a relatively small group of traders.

For brokerage risk teams, the challenge is understanding where losses originate, which trading behaviours contribute to them, and why existing monitoring processes may overlook important warning signs.

Broker Risk Management: Why Individual Account Monitoring Falls Short

Monitoring individual trading accounts can help brokers assess client activity, but it may not provide a complete picture of coordinated strategies operating across multiple accounts or brokers.

Cross-broker hedging, for example, raises questions about how firms identify trading patterns when activity extends beyond their own platforms. Similarly, strategies involving arbitrage or high-frequency trading may require closer examination of how positions are opened, managed and closed.

The risks can be particularly relevant for brokers operating warehoused books, where the broker retains exposure to client trading activity rather than transferring that exposure externally.

Understanding which trader profiles generate the greatest financial exposure, and how losses accumulate over a trading quarter, is therefore an important consideration for brokerage risk management.

Webinar: $5 Million a Quarter in Losses: Where Broker P&L Actually Leaks

In this webinar, Dennis Weissert, CCO at iSAM Securities, will examine where broker losses can arise, how they may become concentrated among particular clients, and why conventional monitoring can fail to identify certain trading behaviours.

The session will cover:

  • Sources of broker P&L losses: How negative balance protection abuse, swap and bonus exploitation, and cross-broker hedging can affect profitability.

  • Limitations of individual account monitoring: Why reviewing accounts separately may fail to identify coordinated trading activity across brokers.

  • Concentration of trading losses: How a small percentage of clients can account for a significant share of a broker's total drawdown.

  • Trader profiles and strategies: The role of high-frequency, arbitrage and martingale trading in brokerage risk exposure.

  • Understanding quarterly losses: What a representative trading quarter can reveal about the activities and client profiles contributing to broker losses.

The discussion will also examine trading behaviours observed by iSAM Securities and the challenges brokers face when assessing their impact on financial performance.

Meet the Speaker: Dennis Weissert, CCO at iSAM Securities

Dennis Weissert is Chief Commercial Officer at iSAM Securities, where his responsibilities include leading the technology strategy across Radar, the firm's broker risk platform, and the Apex bridge.

During the webinar, Weissert will discuss the trading strategies and client behaviours associated with broker P&L losses, drawing on the risk patterns and trader profiles identified by iSAM Securities.

Who Should Attend?

This webinar is relevant to professionals working in:

  • Forex and CFD brokerage operations

  • Brokerage risk management and trading risk

  • Dealing desks and trading operations

  • Broker profitability and P&L management

  • Client trading behaviour monitoring

  • Brokerage management and executive leadership

Whether you oversee trading risk, manage dealing operations or are responsible for brokerage profitability, the session will provide an opportunity to examine the activities that can contribute to financial losses and the challenges involved in identifying them.

Register for the Webinar

Join Finance Magnates and iSAM Securities on 1 December 2026 at 2:00 PM Cyprus Time for a discussion with Dennis Weissert on where broker P&L losses originate, the trading strategies behind them and why conventional monitoring can miss important risks.

Register for the webinar here to reserve your free place.

title: Gold Price Prediction as $4,067 Support Faces Test Ahead of December Rally
summary: Gold is facing a critical technical hurdle in its recovery, as buyers try to hold onto the support level above $4,000.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XAU

Gold is facing a critical technical hurdle in its recovery, as buyers try to hold onto the support level above $4,000.

The precious metal has rallied to its $4,100 range, but current selling activity has put the recovery path at the mercy of a new price floor. Traders are keeping a close watch on nearby support or lack thereof heading into the U.S. inflation data.

In the meantime, gold is set to move next with the help of technical levels, which were identified by analyst James Stanley. The $4067 and $4021 levels may decide if the recent rally can turn into a more substantial recovery this month as it heads into December.

Gold Faces Further Downside Pressure as Fed Rate Hike Bets Strengthen

Gold prices continue to be weighed down by dropping to $4,047.10 an ounce following tougher-than-expected U.S. inflation data and Federal Reserve comments that were hawkish. Gold fell $79.70 or 1.93% to approach its lowest levels since November, as depicted on the Trading Economics chart.

It has also lost significant ground from its January highs above $5,400, in a trend that has seen the price of the metal fall over the majority of 2026. The move on Tuesday adds to the bearish sentiment, as investors reevaluate the Fed’s interest rate trajectory.

Meanwhile, US inflation data have bolstered expectations for monetary policy tightening. Headline inflation slowed to 0.4% month-on-month in October from 0.6% in September but remained above the 0.3% market forecast. Inflation excluding core foods remained steady at 0.3% for the third month in a row, up from an anticipated rate of 0.2%.

The underlying price pressures continue to persist, meaning that the Federal Reserve is having trouble finding any room to consider monetary easing, according to these figures. Support for another rate hike increases pressure on gold, with Christopher Waller suggesting a 50-basis-point move in December.

From a technical standpoint, gold has immediate support at the $4,000 level and could break further to reveal lower support levels. Source: TradingEconomics

It indicates that the price has failed to make any new bullish gains above the $4200 level since September. Sellers may be able to recover at $4,100 to $4,200, where resistance is found. But if the strike continues to hold above this area, it will offer some short-term relief. The bullion’s price is still being held by high interest rate prospects and inflationary pressures for the time being.

$4,021 support and $4,000 remain important downside levels

Analyst James Stanley marked $4,067 as support that is nearby and $4,021 below that. These levels provide two important areas for monitoring selling pressure. If gold can hold up on the defense of $4,067, it’s likely to be able to try to recover again. Buyers would have to generate more upward movement to confirm that the demand is returning.

The gold price is coming back from a previous dip and is nearing a downward-trending line, as seen in Stanley’s chart. Source: Stanley Via X

But if prices continue to fall below $4,067, the $4,021 area may be vulnerable. This would bring gold nearer to a psychological $4,000 level. The level of the round number is technically important also, as $4,000 was also one of the important reference points previously recovered by Stanley. If there is a breakdown below this region, then the current recovery structure will be weakened.

An earlier period of price declines is also reflected in the chart before the most recent price increases. During that sell-off period, gold was under pressure but has bounced from its recent lows. This means the existing support level should be confirmed by a string of purchases.

A recovery from such a move is likely to be accompanied by a downward move below the support level, which suggests that buyers are taking on the selling pressure that is present. On the other hand, if it persists, it means that the seller is still in control.

Descending resistance creates a breakout setup

A descending resistance line is formed by the X chart, as it indicates a trend of a few lower highs. This is a structure that shows the selling pressure that has taken place after gold’s previous drop. In the meantime, an upward-sloping support line has formed from the recent recovery lows. The two “boundaries” are coming closer together and may set up a breakout opportunity as November goes on.

A breakout to the upside in descending resistance would be a good sign the market is buying. But the breakout would need to be a continuous trade up and not a mere spike above resistance. Then nearby resistance zones need to be broken up, and higher swing highs need to be formed in order for Gold to make a comeback. If that happens, it could bolster the technical argument for a recovery in December.

In his previous analysis, Stanley has mentioned the $4,000 price point. It is a significant milestone after the gold rally, he said. Source: X

But if the price declines in rejection, it may signal that the price has begun another consolidation pattern. Gold could be heading towards $4,067 before reaching $4,021. Further breakdown from the rising support level would further undermine the recovery structure. So, the trend of the upcoming breakout may offer a better guide to what price action may look like in December.

title: Arca Opens to Everyone, Paying People for the AI Sessions They’d Otherwise Throw Away
summary: After invite-only early access, the desktop app from the team behind Brevis is now open to anyone on Mac and Windows.   HONG KONG, November 11, 2026: Arca, a new desktop app from the team behind Brevis, opened to the public today. Arca pays people for the AI sessions they’d otherwise throw away. It ...
content:
After invite-only early access, the desktop app from the team behind Brevis is now open to anyone on Mac and Windows.

HONG KONG, November 11, 2026: Arca, a new desktop app from the team behind Brevis, opened to the public today. Arca pays people for the AI sessions they’d otherwise throw away. It finds the session history their AI tools already keep on their computer, lets them choose which sessions to submit, strips sensitive details on the device before anything is uploaded, and pays for the sessions that are approved. Starting today, anyone can sign up with an email address, with no invite and no waitlist.

Much of today’s knowledge work runs through AI tools. People steer a model through a task, correcting it, throwing out what fails and keeping what holds up. Every one of those sessions leaves a detailed record of real work: the back-and-forth, the dead ends, the fix that finally worked. These records pile up by the thousands on people’s computers, and once the window closes, they’re worth nothing to the person who did the work. Arca gives that work a value.

How it works

Arca works with the AI tools people already use, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Claude Desktop. After installing the app, users see the sessions Arca has found on their machine, past ones included. They pick a session to upload, and Arca anonymises it on their computer before it leaves, then returns a quote range. Users either confirm, which sends the session to review, or withdraw, in which case the upload is deleted. Approved sessions are paid weekly.

Arca only reads sessions that are already on the user’s computer, and it lists everything it finds. Nothing uploads in the background, and nothing leaves the device until the user picks a session and confirms. Before a session is uploaded, Arca strips names, file paths, account details and keys, and further anonymising runs on Arca’s side.

“Every AI session is a record of real thinking and real work, and until now the person who did that work got nothing for it,” said Michael, co-founder and CEO of Brevis. “Arca lets people see what their sessions are worth and decide for themselves what to share. We opened it in small batches first to get the experience right. Today it’s open to everyone.”

Built for real work in any field

Arca is built for anyone who does real work with AI, from code to contract reviews, research and long working conversations. Sessions with Claude Opus and Fable, and with the latest GPT models in Codex, qualify today, with more to come. Very short sessions don’t qualify, and every submission is reviewed before it pays. Users can connect GitHub to strengthen their profile, which can raise the value of their sessions, but it isn’t required.

Arca carries the principle behind Brevis’s verifiable computing work into a new domain: things you can verify are worth more than things you have to trust.

Availability

Arca first opened on October 13 in invite-only early access, admitting users in small batches. With today’s launch, the invite requirement is gone. Users sign up with an email address or a Google account and can start right away. Arca is free to use and available now for Mac and Windows at arca.market.

Through November 30, the Arca Launch Challenge adds $10,000 in prizes on top of regular payouts for approved sessions.

About Arca

Arca pays people for the AI sessions they’d otherwise throw away. The desktop app finds the sessions people’s AI tools already keep, lets them choose what to share, anonymises sessions on the device before upload, and pays for approved sessions. Arca is built by the team behind Brevis. Learn more at arca.market.

About Brevis

Brevis builds verifiable computing infrastructure. Its zero-knowledge proving technology, including the open-source Pico zkVM, lets applications prove the results of complex computations. Learn more at brevis.network.

title: Anthropic IPO Targets Up to $64B as Claude Maker Sets $70–$78 Share Range
summary: Anthropic IPO terms propose $70–$78 shares and up to $64.35B in gross public sales. We explain proceeds, the $26B placement and shareholder control.
content:
Skip to content

Anthropic IPO terms propose $70–$78 shares and up to $64.35B in gross public sales. We explain proceeds, the $26B placement and shareholder control.

Anthropic’s IPO has acquired a price range, and the size of the proposed deal turns it into a major test of appetite for AI shares. The Claude developer’s amended prospectus puts the estimated offering price at $70–$78, with 825 million shares proposed for sale.

Multiplying the share count by the range implies a gross public offering of $57.75 billion–$64.35 billion, before fees and any additional underwriter shares. That is a calculation from the proposed terms, not money already raised and not a final valuation of the entire company.

Anthropic IPO terms bring the financing into focus

The amended SEC prospectus, filed November 10, remains preliminary. “The information in this preliminary prospectus is not complete and may be changed,” it states. The range is therefore a statement of proposed terms, not a completed sale or a promise about the first trading price.

Public-market demand will determine much more than the headline size. Investors will assess the price against the business, the capital it needs and the rights attached to the shares. An impressive fundraising total does not, by itself, establish an attractive return for a new shareholder.

For readers following AI through products rather than stocks, this marks a different kind of evaluation. A useful chatbot can win users without settling what its maker should be worth. The IPO asks investors to put a price on the company’s future cash-generating potential.

Who receives the proceeds matters

Anthropic proposes selling about 801.35 million shares itself, while existing holders would sell approximately 23.65 million. The company receives no proceeds from those holders’ sales. The full offering’s gross value should therefore not be described as cash going entirely into Anthropic’s accounts.

This distinction separates primary capital from secondary liquidity. New company shares can fund the business, while a sale by existing holders changes who owns an existing interest. Both can occur in the same transaction, but they serve different purposes.

When assessing any IPO, investors should also distinguish gross proceeds from net proceeds. Underwriting discounts and other transaction expenses affect how much money the company actually receives. A simple price-times-shares calculation is useful for scale, but it is not a substitute for the prospectus’s proceeds analysis.

The $26 billion strategic placement is separate

The filing also describes a $26 billion Class N private placement involving strategic partners, contingent on completion of the IPO and other conditions. This is a separate financing channel. It should not be folded into the public share count or presented as public-market demand already demonstrated.

Strategic and public investors may have different reasons to participate. A commercial partner may value a durable business relationship alongside a financial return. Public shareholders will primarily need to assess the economic exposure they are purchasing at the offered price.

That does not make strategic capital less real. It means the two sources of funding answer different questions. The existence of a committed partner transaction cannot tell readers how a broadly distributed public float will trade after the listing.

Buying shares does not mean buying control

Anthropic’s planned structure reserves 50.1% of voting power on general shareholder matters for a founder-controlled Class F share. Its Long-Term Benefit Trust would generally appoint a majority of the board. Public investors should understand those arrangements before equating an economic stake with conventional corporate control.

Governance affects how investors can respond if their priorities diverge from management’s. It matters most when difficult decisions arise: the pace of spending, the balance between product development and profitability, or choices about how the business pursues its mission.

A buyer can accept limited influence and still see an attractive investment. The important point is to price the rights actually offered rather than assume that every public listing brings the same shareholder powers. Ownership, voting influence and board appointment rights are related, but distinct.

Product momentum meets a stock-market test

The company has also just announced Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, describing stronger technical capabilities and faster output. That product release offers context for the growth story, though vendor-reported model improvements do not establish future earnings.

BNC’s analysis of the new Claude models and their practical limits examines the technology side. The investment question is how capability improvements translate into customer demand, pricing and the costs of serving that demand.

Better models can make a product more useful. They can also require businesses to keep investing to remain competitive. Investors need evidence about both the value delivered to customers and the economics retained by the provider.

What would change the picture next

The most useful next developments are revised terms, an effective registration statement and eventual confirmation of pricing and completion. Until then, a proposed Nasdaq symbol or an estimated range should not be mistaken for a stock already available in ordinary public trading.

The amended prospectus makes Anthropic’s financing plan more concrete. The decisive market test remains ahead: whether investors accept the price and governance terms, and whether the business can ultimately deliver returns that justify them.

title: Exodus Reports $8.3M Quarterly Loss as Wallet Platform Expands Payments Business
summary: Exodus reported third-quarter revenue of around $32.5 million, up 7%, while swinging to an $8.3 million net loss from a profit a year earlier. The…
content:
TL;DR: Exodus reported third-quarter revenue of around $32.5 million, up 7%, while swinging to an $8.3 million net loss from a profit a year earlier. The wallet company’s expansion into payments and card infrastructure adds a new commercial opportunity but also increases the importance of integration costs and execution.

Exodus built its brand around software that helps people hold and exchange digital assets without relying on a traditional centralized exchange account. Its latest results show that running a wallet business at scale now involves more than downloads and token swaps.

In its November 9 third-quarter report, Exodus said revenue reached about $32.5 million, an increase of roughly 7% year over year. The company nevertheless recorded a net loss of approximately $8.3 million, compared with a net profit of about $17 million a year earlier.

The difference between higher revenue and weaker net income points to costs and accounting items that require as much attention as transaction volume.

Wallet activity remained substantial

Exodus reported around 1.4 million monthly active users and approximately 1.4 million quarterly funded users, reflecting the scale of its consumer product. Those are company-defined measures and may overlap; they should not be added together to imply a larger distinct customer base.

The company also cited roughly $1.1 billion in quarterly swap volume. Transaction volume measures value moved through a service; it is not the same as revenue or profit. The share retained by a platform depends on fees, execution arrangements and the costs of providing the service.

This is a useful distinction across the wallet industry. A product can support heavy activity without retaining a large percentage of the value exchanged. Increased usage can even create more customer-service, compliance and technical costs.

Why payments are part of the strategy

Exodus has been extending its role in the infrastructure around digital payments. Its recent company updates describe a combination involving Baanx and Monavate and a growing emphasis on card and payment services. It has also referenced around 1.6 million active cards and substantial payment volume in the broader business context.

Payment services offer a way to make digital assets useful for routine spending rather than only investment and exchange. But building or combining regulated payment operations brings operational work: issuing relationships, settlement partners, compliance programs, fraud controls and support obligations.

NewsBTC previously covered Visa’s work on stablecoin treasury and settlement infrastructure. Exodus operates in a different part of the market, yet both stories show businesses looking for ways to make digital value move through established financial channels.

Likewise, the growing attention paid to tokenized securities infrastructure reflects a wider focus on how blockchain assets connect with ordinary financial workflows. Neither development should be mistaken for proof that Exodus’s specific payment plans will succeed.

Why the earnings swing matters

Management cited increased general and administrative spending among the pressures on the quarter. As a company moves from a comparatively focused software product toward a broader financial-services platform, staffing, oversight and integration costs can rise before new lines generate consistent returns.

That does not make the strategy inherently flawed. It means the outcome will depend on whether additional services create more durable recurring earnings than they cost to build and operate.

What comes next

The useful measures in future results will include transaction and card activity, net revenue retained from those services, the cost of operating the expanded business and whether losses narrow. Users and investors should also pay attention to security, custody arrangements and regulatory disclosures as more payment services are introduced.

Exodus is showing modest revenue growth alongside a more expensive operating model. The next several quarters will help determine whether its payments ambitions create a stronger business or simply add complexity to an already competitive wallet market.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: After the World Cup Spike, Prediction Markets Turn to Brokers to Keep Users Trading
summary:

As prediction markets evolve, the key issu...
content:
2026-11-11T13:45:50.371+02:00

Wednesday, 11/11/2026 | 11:45 GMT by Paul Golden

  • Paul Golden explores how prediction market operators are using broker partnerships, entertainment and social reach to attract new customers and build lasting trading activity.
  • From the World Cup to stock index futures, prediction markets are expanding their product range as platforms compete for liquidity, repeat traders and a stronger position in financial markets.

As momentum shifts between prediction market platforms and the realisation dawns that some of the summer's growth was event-driven rather than sustained, we look at how providers are navigating increasingly uneven growth through distribution and market mix.

As prediction markets evolve, the key issue for operators is less how to attract users during major news events and more how to turn event-driven interest into sustained trading activity.

London's trading industry is coming home!

From Event-Driven Hype to Long-Term Growth

One of the most significant developments in this space in recent months is that sport has become a major volume engine and exposed the limits of event-led growth. Trading activity surged around the 2026 World Cup, with combined volume for Kalshi and Polymarket and its US platform reaching $50.6 billion in July before falling 14.5% to $45.3 billion in August.

The lesson here is that major sporting events can attract enormous activity, but the subsequent fall shows why operators need more than a calendar of headline events.

Entertainment markets have emerged as a customer acquisition opportunity. Kalshi and Polymarket are extending into reality television and popular culture, including shows such as Dancing with the Stars and Love Island.

Kalshi reportedly recorded $5.7 million of volume related to Dancing with the Stars, and its entertainment market volume has increased from $43 million in 2024 to $813 million.

Women are less than 25% of the user base on prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket… but are the largest consumers on Instagram and Facebook. I think Meta’s prediction market product will actually be a huge hit due to this untapped audience and the social/cultural topics they are interested in. Count me in for predicting who gets voted out next on Love Island. 🏝️

— Brit Morin 🦞 (@brit) July 7, 2026

This matters because entertainment can reach people who have little interest in elections, macroeconomic forecasts or conventional financial trading. It also offers recurring weekly events, rather than relying entirely on one-off spectacles.

Brokerages are becoming powerful distribution channels. Robinhood reported $156 million in event contract revenue in Q2 2026, more than ten times the figure for the same period last year. It handled 13.6 billion event contracts during the quarter, also more than ten times the volume recorded in Q1 2025.

In August, Kalshi announced a partnership with brokerage infrastructure provider Alpaca to distribute event contracts through brokerage infrastructure. Last month, it announced an integration with Public (an agentic brokerage), linking event contracts to customers' portfolios and AI-powered investing tools.

The strategic shift is from persuading consumers to download another specialist app to placing prediction markets where they already invest.

We have also seen platforms expand beyond conventional event contracts. In early October, Kalshi announced a stock index perpetual future, broadening its product range beyond contracts tied to discrete events.

This is evidence of convergence between prediction markets and derivatives as operators seek more reasons for users to return between major news events. It also creates a clearer distinction between forecasting a particular outcome and maintaining continuous market exposure.

Meanwhile, regulation and market integrity have become more important competitive factors. In the US, disputes over whether sports-related event contracts fall under federal derivatives oversight or state gambling laws continue, with the NFL backing a request for a US Supreme Court review.

In the UK, the FCA is reportedly engaging with Kalshi and Polymarket as they consider market entry.

For operators, regulatory clarity, reliable settlement, clear rules and credible safeguards are not just compliance costs – they can influence whether mainstream brokers and customers are willing to participate.

Five Strategies to Win and Retain Customers

So which customer acquisition strategies are proving most successful? These can be broken down into five categories:

  • Integration into existing financial apps

  • Owning the moments people already care about

  • Offering breadth, not just one headline market

  • Using social distribution, public probabilities and community

  • Investing in liquidity and a better trading experience

The appeal of integrating with existing financial apps is a lower-friction customer journey due to accounts, identity checks, funding arrangements and trading interfaces already being in place.

Customers can discover event contracts without starting a separate financial relationship, while providers benefit from lower incremental acquisition costs, access to an existing funded user base and cross-selling between equities, options, crypto and event contracts.

Sports tournaments, elections, central bank decisions, economic releases and reality TV finales create natural spikes in attention. Contracts tied to these events are easy to explain and have an obvious deadline. Best execution can be achieved by building a calendar of recurring events, offering markets with clear settlement criteria and retaining users by connecting one event to the next.

I have a million questions about prediction markets, and I understand things through drawing. So I sat down with the CEO of @Kalshi (@mansourtarek_) to better understand how prediction markets actually work, the counter-intuitive impact of prediction markets on elections, and why he believes they can make the world a better place. We cover: - How a prediction market works (hint: a lot like the NYSE) - 60¢ = 60%: how event contracts price probability - Prediction markets vs. the stock exchange vs. sportsbooks - Defining gambling and markets - Why he's in favor of federal regulation - Polls vs. markets: skin in the game & the pursuit of truth - Why markets reward the boring take - What you can't trade on (no wildfire markets) - Hedging 101 at the ice cream shop - Goku, growing up in Lebanon & the 120% rule Highlights: (00:00) Gambling, markets and their historically flirtatious relationship (00:34) Opening Kalshi for the first time (01:19) How a contract works: 60¢ = 60% odds (02:10) Why not just use the stock market? CFTC & derivatives (02:58) Prediction markets vs. sportsbooks: who sets the price (04:35) Where the gambling line is, according to Tarek (05:30) In favor of federal regulation (06:17) The vision: free markets in pursuit of truth (06:39) Why polls miss & markets don't (2016, 2024, Mamdani) (07:24) Echo chambers, hot takes & rewarding the boring take (08:15) What you can't trade on & why (08:54) Hedging 101 at the ice cream shop (10:17) Goku, Lebanon & the 120% rule Our first ever longform @chartsncrafts episode - the first of many.

— Natalie Fratto (@NatalieFratto) November 3, 2026

A sports-first customer may subsequently trade entertainment, politics, weather or economic outcomes, while a financial trader may be interested in interest rates, inflation or equity market outcomes. The strategic benefit is that users can move between categories as their interests change, while the platform retains their account and trading history.

A point to note here is that the number of listed markets does not always equate to greater choice. Markets need sufficient liquidity, competitive pricing and dependable resolution to convert browsing into repeat participation.

Prediction markets naturally generate shareable content, for example, a probability that a candidate will win, inflation will exceed a threshold or a particular team will prevail.

Publishing live market probabilities, explainers and changes in consensus can bring in people who are interested in the forecast before they are ready to trade. Public's integration of event data with portfolio analysis and AI agents illustrates how forecasting information can also be marketed as an investing tool.

The caveat here is that social reach is not proof of profitable acquisition. Public evidence is less conclusive on which referral programmes, influencers or community features generate the best retained customers.

A customer who cannot execute at a reasonable price (or cannot understand how a contract settles) is unlikely to return. Tight spreads, depth, fast execution and clear rules make a platform more useful and credible.

This creates a reinforcing effect whereby more customers can attract more liquidity, which improves the experience for subsequent customers. But it also creates a barrier for new entrants trying to compete against established venues.

For this approach, providers need to measure spreads, depth at relevant prices, fill rates, slippage, settlement disputes and customer retention by market category.

The clearest measurable results appear to be in brokerage distribution and event-driven trading. Longer-term retention is harder to establish from publicly reported volume figures.

title: Cardano Price Prediction: ADA Tests $0.17 Support as $0.21 Breakout Becomes Key
summary: Cardano (ADA) is testing critical support near $0.17 as bearish pressure persists, while traders watch for a potential recovery toward key resistance levels.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: ADA

Cardano (ADA) is testing critical support near $0.17 as bearish pressure persists, while traders watch for a potential recovery toward key resistance levels.

Cardano price is starting the week under pressure, but the latest decline has pushed ADA back into an area where several technical setups are beginning to overlap. According to Brave New Coin, ADA is trading near $0.18, down around 2.13% over the past 24 hours, with daily volume near $176 million.

ADA Weekly Structure Keeps $0.166- $0.142 Support in Focus

Cardano’s weekly chart shows price returning to the same broad region that supported the market during the earlier 2026 decline. ADA price is trading near $0.177, below the $0.189 level that previously acted as support and well underneath the 21-week EMA around $0.213.

Drini’s chart leaves the next support around $0.1667, followed by a deeper level near $0.1423. That lower area is particularly interesting because another test would bring ADA back toward the previous cycle low, creating the possibility of a larger double-bottom structure if buyers respond again.

Cardano is approaching a deeper weekly support region, with $0.166-$0.142 forming the main downside area while $0.189-$0.213 remains the first recovery zone. Source: Drini via X.

The recovery side remains demanding. Reclaiming $0.189 would be the first improvement, but ADA would still need to move through roughly $0.213 before the weekly trend begins to look stronger. Beyond that, $0.235 and $0.283 remain the larger resistance levels visible on the chart.

ADA Facing Active Resistance at $0.21

The lower-timeframe structure offers a slightly more constructive signal. Cardano recently swept beneath the $0.19 range low before moving back inside the broader trading range, showing that buyers were willing to respond once liquidity below support was taken.

That reaction alone has not changed the trend. The chart shared by AllCryptoGems still shows a sequence of lower highs, with approximately $0.21 marking the most important one buyers need to break. Until ADA moves through that level, sellers retain control of the short-term structure despite the recovery from the lows.

A break above $0.21 would be the first meaningful shift and could reopen the larger range toward $0.26. Failure there, however, would leave the $0.19 area vulnerable to another test and increase the risk that the recent liquidity sweep develops into a broader breakdown instead of a reversal.

ADA has reclaimed the $0.19 range low, but a break above the lower high near $0.21 is still needed. Source: AllCryptoGems via X.

Cardano RSI Near Oversold Levels

Momentum is also beginning to reach levels where a reaction becomes more likely. On the daily chart, ADA has fallen back toward $0.175 while the RSI is hovering close to the oversold region after declining steadily alongside price.

The latest reading does not confirm a bottom, but it does show that much of the recent downside momentum has already been absorbed. RSI is now approaching levels that previously pushed stronger Cardano reactions, giving buyers more room to attempt a recovery if selling begins to slow.

A bounce in RSI without an improvement in market structure would remain only a momentum reset, while a recovery in both price and RSI would provide better evidence that the latest decline is beginning to exhaust itself.

Cardano’s daily RSI is approaching oversold territory. Source: Sssesbi via X.

Cardano Staking Reaches 57% of ADA Supply

Cardano’s price remains under pressure, but network participation has stayed remarkably firm. Data highlighted by Bitcoin China, citing Coinbase, shows that roughly 57% of ADA’s circulating supply is currently staked, meaning more than half of the available tokens remain committed to the network even as price trades near recent lows.

That matters because the staking trend is moving very differently from price. ADA has been falling, but holders have not responded by withdrawing heavily from the network. Instead, a large portion of supply remains locked, suggesting that longer-term participation has held up despite the weakness in the market.

The effect could grow more important if demand improves. With a meaningful share of ADA already committed to staking, stronger buying interest would be competing for a smaller liquid portion of supply, potentially giving a future recovery more room to develop if the technical structure begins to turn.

For now, staking is not enough to reverse the bearish chart on its own, but it does show that the weakness in price has not translated into the same deterioration in network participation.

Cardano Support and Resistance Levels

Cardano is now trading close to the lower end of its recent structure, which makes the nearby support levels more important than the larger upside targets for now. The first area to watch sits around $0.166-$0.17, while a deeper breakdown would bring the $0.142 region back into focus.

Cardano price is trading around $0.18, down 2.13% in the last 24 hours. Source: Brave New Coin

On the upside, ADA first needs to recover $0.189 before the short-term picture begins to improve. The more important resistance remains around $0.21-$0.213, where the recent lower high and weekly 21 EMA converge. A break above that area would shift attention toward $0.235, followed by the broader $0.26-$0.28 resistance zone.

Final Thoughts: Can ADA Recover $0.50 in Q4 2026?

Cardano is entering the next part of Q4 from a weak position, but the setup is not without a recovery path. Price is testing an area where RSI is approaching oversold levels, the recent range lows have already attracted a reaction, and staking participation remains strong despite the broader decline.

The first step is simply rebuilding the structure. ADA needs to hold the current support region and start reclaiming the levels lost during the latest selloff, particularly $0.21-$0.213. A move through $0.235 and then $0.26-$0.28 would show that the recovery is developing into something more meaningful rather than another short-lived bounce.

From there, the broader Cardano Price Prediction can begin looking higher. A sustained recovery through the upper-$0.20s would reopen the path toward $0.30-$0.35, and only after those levels are reclaimed would $0.50 become a realistic Q4 extension target.

title: eToro Q3 Profit Drops 74% as Crypto Trading Activity Slows
summary: eToro reported third-quarter net income of about $15 million, down from $57 million a year earlier, as crypto-related activity weakened. Its…
content:
TL;DR: eToro reported third-quarter net income of about $15 million, down from $57 million a year earlier, as crypto-related activity weakened. Its funded-account base continued to grow, highlighting the difference between attracting customers and generating trading revenue from them in any particular quarter.

A trading platform can gain users even when the market becomes less profitable to trade. That tension runs through eToro’s latest financial results, which showed weaker quarterly earnings despite an expanding customer base.

According to the company’s November 10 earnings release, third-quarter net income was approximately $15 million, a decline of about 74% from $57 million in the comparable period. Net contribution came to around $186 million, down 13% year over year, with lower cryptocurrency trading activity contributing to the drop.

At the same time, eToro reported 4.39 million funded accounts, an increase of 18%, and assets under administration of approximately $20.8 billion. It also announced a $250 million share repurchase authorization.

More customers do not guarantee more transactions

Brokerage and trading businesses earn revenue from a mix of activity, product pricing and other services. When customers trade less frequently, a growing account base may not immediately offset the effect. The relationship is particularly visible in crypto, where transaction volumes can shift quickly as market sentiment changes.

That is why the funded-account figure and the net-contribution figure should be assessed together. One shows a measure of customer acquisition and retention; the other gives more insight into the contribution earned from services in the quarter.

Assets under administration are also distinct from eToro’s own cash and corporate assets. They reflect client-related asset values that can be affected by price movements as well as client activity.

What the crypto slowdown does and does not show

Lower crypto activity at one trading platform does not prove digital assets are in a long-term decline. Users may trade through different venues, switch into other asset classes or simply become less active during a choppy period. The business may also earn different amounts from different types of orders.

Still, eToro’s numbers offer an operating-business perspective on the volatility seen in public-market crypto demand. NewsBTC has been tracking recent Bitcoin ETF outflows as well as uneven demand for spot Ether funds. ETF subscriptions and brokerage transaction revenues are separate metrics, but both help describe how investors are participating in the market.

A fall in net contribution can also reflect conditions in noncrypto products. Readers should avoid attributing every change in a diversified platform’s results to Bitcoin prices alone.

What the buyback authorization means

The $250 million repurchase authorization gives eToro permission to buy back shares under its program, subject to the company’s terms. It is not proof that the full amount was repurchased on November 10, nor does it guarantee future share-price gains.

Repurchases can alter the share count and capital allocation over time, but their effect depends on execution price, cash available and how the company balances other investments. They are best evaluated alongside earnings quality and strategic spending.

The next test for eToro

Investors should watch whether funded-account growth leads to sustained activity and improved net contribution in subsequent quarters. The product mix matters: strength in equities or other services could help offset a quieter crypto market, while increased marketing and operating costs could limit the benefit.

For crypto observers, the report is a reminder that adoption and profitability do not always move together. eToro gained funded accounts, but the softer trading environment made it harder to translate that scale into quarterly profit.
