title: Bitdeer Revenue Jumps 89% to $320.7M as AI Backlog Grows Despite Quarterly Loss
summary: Bitdeer posted record third-quarter revenue of $320.7 million, up 89% year over year, while reporting a $125.5 million net loss. Its stated AI-cloud…
content:
TL;DR: Bitdeer posted record third-quarter revenue of $320.7 million, up 89% year over year, while reporting a $125.5 million net loss. Its stated AI-cloud backlog approached $2.9 billion, highlighting demand potential but not revenue already earned or cash already collected.

Bitdeer has delivered one of the clearest examples yet of a Bitcoin mining business trying to transform itself into a provider of broader computing infrastructure. Its latest quarter brought record revenue and a sizable artificial-intelligence cloud order pipeline. It also remained deeply unprofitable under standard accounting measures.

In its November 10 third-quarter results announcement, the company reported $320.7 million in revenue, an 89% increase from the year-earlier period. Adjusted EBITDA rose to about $69.6 million, while the GAAP net loss reached approximately $125.5 million.

Those measures differ, and the gap requires careful reading. Management highlighted changes in the fair value of digital-asset-related borrowing, including a $54.6 million noncash item, as one factor in the accounting result.

A $2.9 billion backlog is not $2.9 billion in the bank

The figure likely to attract the most attention is Bitdeer’s reported AI-cloud backlog of approximately $2.9 billion. A backlog represents contracted or expected future services under the company’s reporting definitions, rather than cash already received or recognized quarterly revenue.

The amount eventually converted into sales will depend on contract delivery, customer demand, capacity coming online and the terms attached to commitments. Investors should seek disclosures about timing and any conditions that could delay or reduce the total.

Nevertheless, a substantial backlog can signal customer interest for specialized infrastructure. That is particularly valuable in a business where constructing or equipping data centers involves significant upfront spending.

Bitcoin mining still matters to the numbers

Bitdeer reported production of 3,855 Bitcoin during the quarter and said it held 47 Bitcoin at quarter-end. Those figures help distinguish operating output from Bitcoin retained on the balance sheet. Production can be high even if a firm sells most of the coins to fund operations, equipment or other projects.

The company also reported approximately $213.7 million in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash. A cash balance should be considered alongside capital commitments, financing costs and planned expansion rather than treated as unencumbered profits from AI.

NewsBTC has reported on Riot’s decision to sell Bitcoin as it pursues major AI infrastructure contracts. The miners are pursuing different projects, but both illustrate a sector balancing near-term funding needs with investments that may generate future revenue.

Our coverage of Soluna and Bitdeer’s Texas infrastructure agreement adds a concrete example of why access to powered sites and commercial partnerships remains important as the competition for computing capacity grows.

Why the loss cannot be ignored

Adjusted EBITDA may help investors evaluate operating performance before certain expenses and valuation changes. It is not identical to net income or free cash flow. A company can report a positive adjusted measure and still incur losses, financing costs and heavy investment requirements.

That is why the $125.5 million net loss deserves to stand alongside the $320.7 million revenue headline. Both are true, and neither alone gives a complete picture.

The next test is execution

Bitdeer’s next reporting periods need to show when AI-cloud backlog turns into delivered services, how those services contribute to margins and how much capital they consume. Improvements in mining efficiency and power costs will also remain relevant.

The latest results point to striking revenue momentum and a potentially meaningful new business line. They do not yet demonstrate that the shift toward AI has resolved the financial volatility historically associated with Bitcoin mining.

Since the start of Q4, the crypto market has continued to weaken amid volatility. Major asset prices have pulled back from their highs, and market participants have become more cautious. As the market cools, HTX has focused its efforts on solidifying its trading fundamentals and offering diverse yield generation pathways. In October, HTX saw a significant overall improvement in the market depth of its core spot trading pairs, with the 0.05% depth for the BTC/USDT pair increasing by 78%. At the end of October, HTX Earn launched the APY Boost Promotion as part of the HTX Winter Campaign, delivering stable yield options for users amid fluctuating market conditions.

Overall Spot Depth Enhancement, Ensuring Smoother Execution for Large-Volume Trades

In October, HTX continued to strengthen its collaboration with professional market makers, improving market-making support, order book depth, and the overall trading environment, which contributed to an overall improvement in the market depth of its core spot trading pairs. Taking BTC/USDT as an example, the pair’s 0.01% depth increased by 42% in October, while its 0.05% depth jumped by 78%. Deeper market depth ensures that orders of the same size have a smaller price impact, allowing large-volume trades to be executed closer to market price. For core assets like BTC, this means users can easily execute trades even during periods of severe market volatility.

Centered around the two core assets of BTC and ETH, HTX also rolled out a series of trading rewards in October, including trading challenges, fee rebates, trading lucky draws, and iPhone Duo theme activities, with the flagship trading challenge attracting over 10,000 participants.

Asset Matrix Continues to Expand, Stock Trading Assets Reach 307 Types

In October, HTX Futures launched 40 new assets, including 29 selected stocks and ETFs alongside 11 crypto assets. To date, the platform’s number of stock trading assets has grown to 307, covering core US stocks, major global indices and ETFs, biopharmaceuticals, energy infrastructure, and Asia-Pacific market leaders. Overall platform liquidity and user activity have both reached new highs.

This month’s new listings focused on sectors including AI computing power and hardware innovation, biopharmaceuticals and healthcare, mass consumption and high-dividend blue chips, as well as Asia-Pacific core markets and frontier technologies. Targets such as STMicroelectronics (STM), United Microelectronics (UMC), Synopsys (SNPS), Constellation Energy (CEG), Pfizer (PFE), Boeing (BA), Procter & Gamble (PG), McDonald’s (MCD), Starbucks (SBUX), Indonesia Index ETF (EIDO), and Taiyo Yuden (TAIYOYUDEN) were rolled out in succession, offering a balanced mix of growth-oriented tech stocks and defensive assets like consumer goods and pharmaceuticals.

As HTX continues to expand its asset offerings, cumulative TradFi trading volume has surpassed $7.5 billion, with $1.5 billion added in October alone.

In the spot asset category, new listings introduced by HTX in October primarily centered around the AI sector, featuring projects such as POD, AXIS, DNA, and NMR. Notably, Axis Robotics (AXIS), which focuses on physical AI and robotics training data, was jointly launched as a primary listing by HTX, surging by up to 37% following its debut.

HTX Earn Offers APY Boost on 7 Products, USDT Loan Rates Maintain Strong Competitiveness

In October, user interest in HTX Earn continued to rise. SVIP Flexible subscriptions among users with large holdings remained exceptionally popular, with participating users increasing by 16.1% month-on-month and subscription volume surging by over 20% month-on-month.

On October 31, HTX Earn launched an APY Boost Promotion as part of the HTX Winter Campaign. The promotion offers APY boosts on 7-day fixed products featuring an APY of up to 10% for three mainstream coins (BTC, ETH, TRX) and four stablecoins (USDT, USDC, USDS, USDD). Each user can subscribe for up to 2 million USDT worth of each respective asset in the 7-day fixed product for that asset. By subscribing to all seven assets, a user can access a combined  boosted APY quota of up to approximately 14 million USDT, fully accommodating the asset allocation needs of users with large holdings. After the products mature, users can subscribe again, ensuring strong liquidity for their funds.

In terms of borrowing, HTX’s USDT loan interest rates maintained robust competitiveness across the industry. In October, the platform’s annualized USDT loan interest rate ranged from 4.75% to 5.3%, with discounted rates for large-volume borrowers as low as 3.84%, empowering users to unlock the capital potential of their holdings at lower costs. During the HTX Margin Autumn Craze, USDT loan scale grew by 18.6% month-on-month, and margin trading volume surged by over 128%. Currently, the HTX Margin Trading & Borrowing Bonanza Month is underway and will run through November 25, offering 7 tiers of rewards for USDT loans alongside up to a 50% fee rebate on trades during the Margin Trading Contest.

In the OTC sector, HTX has continued to expand payment channels for its OTC Desk, partnering with multiple payment providers to further optimize the user trading experience and reduce transaction costs.

$HTX Q3 Burn Performance Shines, TOKEN2049 Spotlights Brand Influence

On October 15, HTX DAO completed its $HTX token burn for Q3 2026. A total of approximately 9.39 trillion $HTX tokens were burned, valued at roughly $15.48 million, representing a quarter-over-quarter burn volume increase of approximately 25.6%. This brings the cumulative total of $HTX burned and pledged to 127.17 trillion tokens to date. Under HTX DAO’s established mechanism, HTX acts as an ecosystem partner, dedicating 50% of its quarterly revenues to $HTX buybacks and burns.

At the VIP private dinner, the HTX team engaged in deep dialogues with industry representatives, ecosystem contributors, and partners, exchanging viewpoints on industry evolution, market shifts, and product experiences to foster mutual understanding while optimizing services and expanding collaborations.

Standing by Users Through Every Market Cycle

Markets fluctuate. Facing market ups and downs, what the platform can do for users is deliver a better trading experience with each transaction, introduce valuable innovative products and practical rewards, and firmly safeguard user asset security. Compliance is the foundation of all these efforts. In October, HTX continued to deepen constructive communication with relevant regulatory authorities and work toward the proper resolution of relevant matters, while further strengthening its compliance measures. These efforts create more favorable conditions for focusing on user services and pursuing long-term development. Over the past 13 years, HTX has weathered market cycles one after another alongside users worldwide. title: HIVE Reports $84.9M Revenue as AI GPU Business Grows 71% Amid Mining Pressures
summary: HIVE Digital reported $84.9 million in fiscal second-quarter revenue and roughly 71% growth in its AI-focused BUZZ GPU business. The company also…
content:
TL;DR: HIVE Digital reported $84.9 million in fiscal second-quarter revenue and roughly 71% growth in its AI-focused BUZZ GPU business. The company also recorded a substantial quarterly loss, including a mining-equipment impairment. The results show both the promise and cost of shifting computing capacity toward AI services.

Bitcoin miners have spent much of 2026 trying to turn their access to electricity, land and data centers into businesses that can serve more than one market. HIVE Digital’s latest numbers put a price tag on that strategy.

The company said its fiscal second quarter, ended September 30, 2026, brought in approximately $84.9 million of revenue. Its BUZZ high-performance-computing division generated about $8.8 million, an increase of 70.7% from the comparable period. HIVE also reported about $139 million in cash on the balance sheet.

The growth is meaningful, but the AI arm remains far smaller than the company’s combined operations. A rapidly growing new division does not automatically replace the economics of Bitcoin mining.

The headline loss tells the other half

HIVE reported a quarterly net loss in the region of $78 million and included a mining-equipment impairment of approximately $31.2 million. Impairments are generally noncash accounting charges in the period they are recorded, but they can still indicate that expected future economic value has fallen.

That distinction is important. A loss containing a major impairment is not the same as the business spending an identical amount of cash in the quarter. Equally, treating impairments as irrelevant would miss what they say about the pressure on older machines or assumptions about their earning potential.

Mining hardware has a useful life shaped by electricity prices, network difficulty, equipment efficiency and Bitcoin’s market value. When those assumptions change, a fleet that looked attractive two years ago may not justify its former carrying value.

AI capacity does not arrive free

The case for AI data centers is that demand for specialized computing may offer a revenue stream less closely tied to Bitcoin’s mining difficulty. But supplying GPU services requires capital, customer relationships, network infrastructure and operational expertise different from the work of running application-specific mining rigs.

NewsBTC has tracked miners making that transition, including Riot’s Bitcoin sales alongside its AI-data-center ambitions. HIVE’s BUZZ expansion is another version of the same strategic question: how quickly can an established miner earn durable income from compute services?

Partnerships and infrastructure projects are relevant here too. Our reporting on TeraWulf’s growth in AI leasing shows how the business of securing power-intensive sites and monetizing them through leases has become competitive. Possessing a data center does not guarantee demand for the GPUs housed in it.

What to measure in the next quarter

Future reports should clarify how much revenue the AI division earns, whether its margins justify continued capital investment and how the mining segment performs as difficulty changes. Total company revenue can rise or fall for reasons unrelated to the profitability of the new computing business.

Investors should also watch the company’s liquidity, debt commitments and equipment spending. The $139 million cash figure is helpful context, but not a substitute for understanding cash consumption and future construction obligations.

HIVE is presenting itself as a dual-engine business. The latest quarter demonstrates that GPU services are growing quickly, while the bottom-line loss shows why the transition remains a work in progress rather than an accomplished turnaround.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: CoreWeave Earnings Hit $3.66B as AI Demand Surges—but the Interest Bill Grows
summary: CoreWeave earnings show surging AI demand, but a $709M loss and rising interest costs keep financing in focus. Here is what the results reveal.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: CRWV NVDA

CoreWeave earnings show surging AI demand, but a $709M loss and rising interest costs keep financing in focus. Here is what the results reveal.

CoreWeave earnings delivered the growth number AI investors wanted and the interest bill they still have to confront. Quarterly revenue reached $3.661 billion, but a $709 million net loss showed why booming demand for computing capacity does not automatically translate into profits for the companies supplying it.

The November 10 results offer a concrete answer to one part of the AI debate: customers are spending. The harder question is whether the infrastructure can be financed and operated on terms that leave enough value for shareholders after lenders are paid.

CoreWeave earnings beat revenue expectations

The company’s results release reports revenue up from $1.365 billion a year earlier. Reuters put the analyst consensus at $3.55 billion, so the result exceeded that benchmark. Comparisons elsewhere can differ slightly because estimates come from different data providers.

“This was a breakout quarter for CoreWeave,” chief executive Michael Intrator said in the release. He highlighted an expected approximately $9 billion of customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months as one of several funding sources.

That expectation is relevant to the financing debate, but it remains a forecast. A customer deposit can improve near-term liquidity without being equivalent to profit earned from delivering a service. The company still needs to provide the capacity and meet the obligations attached to its contracts.

The interest bill is the tension

CoreWeave reported $207 million of operating income against $846 million of net interest expense. Its adjusted EBITDA was $2.256 billion. The difference between those measures is central to reading the quarter: adjusted EBITDA strips out costs that remain important to an infrastructure business and its investors.

Operating income measures the business after operating expenses. Net interest expense reflects the cost of financing. A positive operating result can therefore coexist with a large net loss when financing and other items absorb the operating profit.

The comparison does not establish that the business cannot become profitable. It establishes the hurdle that growth must clear. Investors who focus only on revenue risk overlooking how much of the benefit flows to providers of capital before reaching ordinary shareholders.

Backlog is a promise to deliver

The company reported approximately $132.5 billion in revenue backlog. Its definition includes committed customer-contract amounts subject to delivery and service-availability requirements. It is future business to execute, not cash already earned.

A long backlog can make investment planning more credible because it gives management evidence of demand. It can also create a demanding construction and deployment schedule. Servers, power and facilities must be available when customers require them, and financing has to bridge the gap between spending and collecting revenue.

For investors, the useful question is therefore not simply whether backlog increased. It is how efficiently contracted demand turns into operating cash and earnings. Delays or higher funding costs can change that conversion even when the customer relationship remains intact.

Guidance raises the stakes again

CoreWeave raised its full-year revenue outlook to $13 billion–$13.3 billion. It expects fourth-quarter interest expense of $1.05 billion–$1.15 billion. Those two forecasts frame the next test: continued growth alongside a substantial financing burden.

The guidance should not be read as a guarantee. Investors will need to compare actual delivery and funding outcomes with management’s expectations when the next results arrive. A revenue forecast can improve while the eventual return on invested capital remains an open question.

BNC’s earlier assessment of Wall Street’s argument that the AI sell-off was overdone identified earnings as an important test. CoreWeave now supplies evidence for both sides: strong sales for the optimists, and meaningful funding costs for the sceptics.

Why this matters beyond one AI stock

The wider AI investment case depends on several links working together. Model developers must attract paying users; cloud operators must supply computing capacity; and infrastructure owners must earn enough to support the capital required. Success at one link does not automatically settle the economics of the others.

That distinction also matters when comparing businesses exposed to data centres. A supplier selling equipment, a landlord leasing powered buildings and a cloud company renting computing services can benefit from the same trend while carrying very different financing risks.

CoreWeave’s results make those differences easier to see. Rapid revenue growth is evidence of demand for its services. The interest line is evidence of the price of building the platform that meets that demand. Neither figure should be used to erase the other.

The next disclosures worth watching are actual customer payments, the conversion of backlog into delivered services and the relationship between operating earnings and financing costs. These offer a more durable test than a single session’s share-price move.

CoreWeave has strengthened the case that AI infrastructure demand is real. It has not yet removed the question that made this earnings report so consequential: how much that growth will ultimately be worth after paying to finance it.

title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Carbon as Its Strongest Model for Autonomous AI Agents
summary: Google has begun a wider rollout of Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier AI model designed to handle complex agentic workflows that require sustained reasoning and repeated verification.
content:
Skip to content

Google has begun a wider rollout of Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier AI model designed to handle complex agentic workflows that require sustained reasoning and repeated verification.

The release expands access to Google’s most capable model for demanding software engineering, cybersecurity, scientific research, and knowledge work. It also introduces a new multi-agent coordination feature in Google Antigravity, allowing specialized AI agents to work together on complex projects.

Gemini 4 Carbon Targets Complex Agentic Workflows

Google DeepMind describes Gemini 4 Carbon as its strongest model for long-horizon tasks, where completing a request requires multiple stages of planning, execution, testing, and refinement. Unlike conventional AI assistants that primarily respond to individual prompts, Carbon is designed to maintain context across extended workflows and verify its work before producing a final result.

Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon, its most powerful model yet, designed for complex workflows and advanced multi-step reasoning. Source: Google via X

Koray Kavukcuoglu, senior vice president of Google DeepMind and Google’s chief AI architect, described Carbon as the company’s “strongest model with frontier performance in cybersecurity capabilities and long-horizon agentic workflows.”

The model builds on Gemini 4 Argon but uses more reasoning tokens to investigate problems, evaluate possible solutions, and perform additional verification rounds. Google says this approach makes Carbon better suited to complex coding and debugging, open-ended scientific research, and engineering projects that require coordination across multiple tools.

However, Google maintains that Argon remains a suitable choice for most software engineering and knowledge-work applications. Carbon is intended for more demanding assignments where deeper reasoning and additional verification can justify higher computational requirements.

Gemini 4 Carbon also supports multimodal inputs, including text, images, audio, and video. According to its technical model card, the model has a combined input-output context window of up to one million tokens, allowing it to process extensive information within a single workflow.

Google Antigravity Introduces the /swarm Multi-Agent Feature

A central part of the release is Google’s preview of the /swarm feature in Antigravity, its agent-focused development platform. The feature allows users to turn a single prompt into a coordinated team of specialized AI agents that can divide work, execute tasks simultaneously, and review one another’s output.

Gemini 4 Carbon outperforms Argon on demanding benchmarks, including coding, cybersecurity, and financial tasks, through deeper reasoning and enhanced verification. Source: Google AI via X

The system uses a coordinating agent to distribute responsibilities among parallel workers operating in isolated Git workspaces. Additional verification agents can run tests, inspect proposed changes, and identify potential problems before the work is completed.

Google Antigravity describes the approach as a system in which agents “plan, build, and verify in parallel.” A shared message board and dedicated interface allow developers to monitor the team’s progress, inspect individual agents, and intervene when necessary.

Google demonstrated the system by creating an interactive 3D exhibition of the Eiffel Tower’s construction between 1887 and 1889. Using historical photographs and engineering drawings as references, a team of Gemini 4 Carbon agents generated a Three.js experience that presented the structure’s development through an interactive visualization.

The demonstration highlights Google’s focus on tasks that extend beyond generating code snippets or answering technical questions. Carbon can coordinate multiple stages of development, including building assets, integrating components, testing functionality, and refining the final application.

The /swarm preview is rolling out across the Antigravity application and command-line interface. Google also allows different models to handle different responsibilities, enabling Carbon to perform demanding architectural planning and auditing while faster models manage routine implementation work.

Benchmark Results Highlight Coding, Cybersecurity, and Scientific Reasoning

Google’s published evaluations indicate improvements across several areas of AI performance, particularly agentic coding, cybersecurity, and complex knowledge work.

The company reports that Gemini 4 Carbon ranks first on CursorBench 4.0, Perplexity’s WANDR, and Zapier’s AutomationBench. Google also says the model achieves more than twice the cost efficiency per task compared with the next-best external model across these evaluations.

Gemini 4 Carbon is Google’s strongest model, built for complex, long-horizon tasks across software engineering, cybersecurity, science, and knowledge work. Source: Google DeepMind via X

A separate assessment focuses on the Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark, developed in partnership with Artificial Analysis. The evaluation examines how AI agents process visually complex information, including charts, engineering diagrams, spreadsheets, and documents, before producing professional work.

The benchmark contains 200 tasks developed with domain experts across 10 industries and 83 occupations. Each assignment represents a multi-step project designed to reflect work that could take an experienced professional between three and eight hours to complete.

Gemini 4 Carbon ranked second in overall quality in the MKA evaluation while completing tasks at approximately one-sixth of the average cost of the highest-scoring model. The result highlights its ability to balance output quality with the computational expenses associated with complex AI workflows.

Cybersecurity is another important focus of the release. Google’s model card reports scores of 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro, 54.8% on ExploitGym, and 71% on CWE-bench. These evaluations cover different stages of vulnerability discovery, exploitation, and patching.

Google initially restricted access to Carbon’s specialized cybersecurity capabilities through its Fairwind Program, which provides access to verified security defenders. The company says this approach supports defensive research while maintaining safeguards against potential misuse.

Despite these improvements, Google acknowledges that protection against sophisticated prompt-injection attacks remains an area requiring continued development. The company says it is expanding automated security testing and strengthening safeguards alongside the model’s capabilities.

Gemini 4 Carbon Availability and Pricing

Gemini 4 Carbon became available more broadly on November 10, following its initial announcement on October 28 and an earlier limited rollout to cybersecurity defenders.

Developers can access the model through the paid Gemini API tier in Google AI Studio and Android Studio. Enterprise customers can use it through Gemini for business, while Google AI Ultra subscribers are receiving access through the Gemini app, Google Antigravity, and AI Mode in Search.

Google is also expanding access for scientific research. Eligible researchers can apply to use Carbon and Argon through Antigravity’s highest usage tier without charge for six months, subject to selection, capacity, and program requirements.

For API customers, Google has introduced an initial pricing structure of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, matching the introductory rates previously offered for Gemini 4 Argon. These rates remain in effect through November 30, 2026, before increasing to $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens from December 1.

The launch positions Gemini 4 Carbon as a specialized option for developers, businesses, and researchers working on complex projects that demand sustained AI reasoning and coordinated execution. With the addition of /swarm, Google is also extending its development platform toward multi-agent systems in which multiple AI models can collaborate on larger assignments rather than relying on a single agent to complete every step.
